stories.title: SP worker holds half-naked protest:Submits memorandum to SHO, demands fertiliser supply for farmers within 15 days
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party workers held a unique protest in Varanasi’s Sigra area on Sunday afternoon, demanding availability of fertilisers for farmers. During the protest, SP worker Harish Mishra expressed his anger by going half-naked and later reached Sigra police station to submit a memorandum addressed to officials. The protest aimed to demand timely availability of essential fertilisers like DAP, urea and potash for farmers and action against alleged black marketing and smuggling of fertilisers. Farmers should get fertilizers on time - Harish During the protest, Harish Mishra said he had come to submit an application regarding farmers’ issues before the concerned officials at Sigra. SP workers Sandeep Yadav and Anil Yadav were also present with him. He alleged that farmers were not getting DAP, urea and potash on time. He claimed that several cooperative societies remained locked, due to which farmers were unable to get fertilisers and paddy sowing was being affected. Harish alleged that farmers were suffering due to alleged middlemen involvement and smuggling of fertilisers. He warned that failure to provide fertilisers on time would severely impact farming and worsen the financial crisis faced by farmers. Fertilizer should be available within 15 days - Harish Harish demanded identification of people involved in alleged smuggling and black marketing of DAP, urea and potash and strict action against them. He said if any departmental official or outside middleman was found involved, legal action should also be taken against them. He also demanded that all cooperative societies should be ensured adequate supply of fertilisers within the next 15 days.

stories.title: 20 girls secretly shifted from Varanasi to Lucknow:MLM company panicked after raid, took ₹30,000 each for training
stories.summary: A gang allegedly duping youths on the pretext of providing jobs and collecting ₹30,000-35,000 from them has been busted by Varanasi Police. The accused allegedly forced victims to recruit new people through a multi-level marketing (MLM) network. After the raid, the gang secretly shifted 20 girls to Lucknow on Saturday night. Lucknow Police received information about them, rescued the girls and handed them over to their families on Sunday. In a joint operation by Varanasi Cyber Crime Police and Rohanian police, 19 people were arrested. Around 200 youths were found undergoing training at the spot, most of them from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh. According to police, they received information that youths were being called to a rented building in Audhe Bachhaon village under Akhari outpost area of Rohania and were being made to do network marketing in the name of Mahadev Enterprises. Took ₹30,000 for joining kit During the raid, around 200 people were found taking training on the first floor, while 19 accused were operating the entire programme. Seeing police, the organisers tried to flee but were caught during a cordon. During questioning, four youths told police that they were promised jobs in offices, agriculture work and companies like Tata with salaries of ₹25,000 per month. They were asked to deposit ₹30,000-32,000 initially. Instead of providing jobs, they were made to attend daily training sessions and were told that they would neither receive salary nor get their money back until they added at least three new members under them. Brainwashed youths to create pyramid chain Main accused Deepak Kumar Shah told police that he had taken a franchise of a direct marketing company through Mahadev Enterprises. He allegedly invited people by promising jobs under the cover of selling company products, collected ₹30,000-35,000 as joining fees and provided low-cost kits in return. The recruits were then trained to expand the network. The accused admitted that youths were psychologically influenced and encouraged to bring in their relatives and friends. Through this method, a pyramid chain was created to continuously earn money from new recruits. Youths from several states became victims According to police, most youths found at the training centre had been brought from different districts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh after being promised good jobs and salaries. Girls shifted to Lucknow after raid After the raid at the Varanasi office, 20 girls were allegedly taken away secretly and brought to Lucknow late on Saturday night. They were kept at a hostel in the Behta area under Gudamba police station. On Sunday morning, one of the girls messaged her family after feeling safe. Their local guardians in Lucknow reached the spot with police, following which the matter came to light. Police said the case is linked to Varanasi and the girls will be handed over to their families. Girls allegedly brainwashed Police said many girls associated with the network had already been influenced. During conversations, they repeatedly said they had come for jobs and were only undergoing training. When asked to return home, they reportedly responded, “What will we do after going home?”

stories.title: Lawyer abusing CJI used to teach:Father says he was struggling financially, mother says son is not criminal
stories.summary: After losing his job, son was struggling with financial problems. To manage his education expenses, he started giving tuition classes. During this period, he became a victim of cyber fraud. Since then, his behaviour had changed, said his father. The statement was made by Surendra Singh Yadav, father of lawyer Prabal Pratap Yadav, who allegedly threw files at judges in the Supreme Court on July 10 and abused while taking the name of Chief Justice of India (CJI). Prabal’s entire family lives in Etawah, while he was staying in Lucknow for his LLB studies. His mother Kunti Devi said she came to know about the incident after watching its video. She said she has called her son’s number several times since then. The phone keeps ringing, but he does not answer. Later, she found out that he was in police custody. “I do not know how he is or what condition he is in. I am very worried. He is not a criminal,” she said. Prabal’s uncle Ravindra Singh Yadav said a complaint regarding the cyber fraud was also filed with the local police and senior officials, but no action was taken. Since then, Prabal had been under mental stress. Meanwhile, he approached the court and was representing himself. Family lives in one-room house in Etawah Prabal Pratap belongs to a simple farming family and their financial condition is not strong. His family lives in Nagla Jaipal village under Bharathana police station area of Etawah, in a house with one room and a verandah. The family owns around two and a half bighas of agricultural land. The walls of the house are not plastered. His father Surendra Singh Yadav works at a shop in Bharathana along with farming, while his mother manages the household. His two sisters, Priya and Sandhya, are married. Joined LLB after completing B.Ed Kunti Devi said Prabal completed his early education from SAV Inter College in Etawah. He later graduated from SS Memorial College and completed B.Ed from Henwara College. Around two years ago, he enrolled in LLB and started living in a rented room near Lucknow University for his studies. She said Prabal had gone to Agra with his uncle in May for his heart operation and later travelled to Delhi from there. She last spoke to him around 6 pm on the day of the incident. He told her that he was going to sleep. After that, she could not contact him. Lost job after allegation of harassing female colleague Villagers said Prabal worked at a software development company in Lucknow’s Vikas Nagar. During this period, he was accused of sending inappropriate and abusive emails to a female colleague. Following the complaint, the company removed him from the job and withheld his salary. Since then, he remained disturbed and under stress. Later, he accused the company of involvement in anti-national activities and approached the court seeking registration of an FIR. Reached Supreme Court after High Court rejected plea It is claimed that last year Prabal filed an application in Lucknow’s CJM court seeking an FIR against the company. The court sought a police report. On February 26, 2026, the court accepted the matter as a private complaint and asked Prabal to submit evidence. On April 6, he approached the Allahabad High Court seeking an order for direct FIR registration by cancelling the complaint case. The High Court rejected his plea, following which Prabal approached the Supreme Court. Villagers say - A youth who stays away from disputes Villagers including Sachin Yadav, Sunil Kumar and Vishal said Prabal was a quiet person who was focused on studies. They said he often advised people to stay away from disputes. They added that he has no criminal record and the news of his behaviour in the Supreme Court has shocked the entire village. 2 pictures of the commotion in the courtroom Now read the entire matter in 4 pointers-

stories.title: 16 dead in UP monsoon, wedding guests' car swept away:Horse cart drowns in underpass; 10-foot crocodile found in field, rain in 5 cities
stories.summary: The spell of monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rain lashed Gorakhpur, Gonda, Bahraich, Deoria and two other cities late on Saturday night. On Sunday morning, skies remained cloudy over Lucknow, Kanpur, Barabanki and most other cities. However, bright sunshine appeared by around 8:30 am. Rain has been forecast in 33 districts today. Heavy rainfall is likely in eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Terai region. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the state received an average of 10.3 mm of rain across 64 cities in the past 24 hours. The normal average for this period is 10.4 mm. Sultanpur recorded the highest rainfall at 63.8 mm, followed by Barabanki with 62.5 mm. Continuous heavy rain in the hills has caused rivers and streams across Uttar Pradesh to swell. The Ganga's water level has started rising in Prayagraj. In Bijnor, water from the Malan River is flowing over a bridge. In Mahoba, a Bolero carrying a wedding party plunged into a drain at around 11 pm on Saturday. Six wedding guests, including the groom's father, were inside the vehicle. Local residents jumped into the drain and rescued all of them. In Meerut, repeated heavy showers during the day left an underpass submerged under nearly 10 feet of water. A horse cart was drowned, killing both the driver and the horse. In Etah, a 10-foot crocodile was found in a paddy field. Villagers, with the help of the Forest Department, captured it. Monsoon may weaken temporarily: Weather scientist Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said: "There are signs that the monsoon is weakening for the time being. This is a completely normal and temporary situation. Rainfall activity will intensify again once a fresh weather system becomes active over the Bay of Bengal or other regions. For now, western Uttar Pradesh may witness a break in monsoon rainfall for the next week. Strong sunshine, rising temperatures and humidity are likely to trouble people." Villagers shoot reels sitting on crocodile after rescue in Etah A large crocodile emerged from waterlogged paddy fields in Maksudpur village of Jalesar area in Etah district. Villagers immediately informed the Forest Department and local police. The crocodile was successfully rescued. Its mouth was tied with a rope before it was placed inside a cage. During the rescue, villagers even sat on the crocodile's back and made social media reels. Regional Forest Officer Girjesh Tiwari said the crocodile had been rescued safely and released in a suitable location. Jalesar Station House Officer Akhilesh Dixit said the crocodile was caught with the help of villagers. See weather visuals from Uttar Pradesh Clear weather returns to Lucknow; city records 20.8 mm rain in 24 hours Clouds covered Lucknow on Sunday morning before sunshine emerged by around 8 am. The Meteorological Department has forecast a maximum temperature of 35°C and a minimum of 27°C today. Winds are also expected to blow at speeds of 10–20 kmph during the day. The state capital received 20.8 mm of rain in the past 24 hours, which is 148% above the normal rainfall of 8.4 mm. From 1 June to 11 July, Lucknow has received 95.8 mm of rainfall, 40% below the normal average of 158.3 mm. Road caves in near Meerut's Zero Mile–Begumpul intersection A road near the Zero Mile–Begumpul intersection in Meerut has caved in following recent heavy rain. The damaged stretch is located close to an underground Metro station and the Namo Bharat (RRTS) station. Wedding party's Bolero swept into drain in Mahoba A Bolero carrying a wedding procession to Banda was swept into the overflowing Shyama drain on Saturday night. The incident occurred near Sirsikala village in the Khanna police station area. Six wedding guests, including the groom's father, were travelling in the vehicle. Hearing their cries for help, nearby residents jumped into the water and rescued all six safely. Heavy overnight rain in Gorakhpur; cloudy morning, more showers forecast Heavy rain lashed Gorakhpur late on Saturday night. The city remained under cloud cover from Sunday morning. Weather scientists said the sky would remain cloudy throughout the day, with intermittent showers likely. The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 32°C and 34°C, while the minimum temperature is likely to stay between 27°C and 28°C. Clear skies in Agra; no rain expected until 17 July The weather remained clear in Agra from Sunday morning, with bright sunshine. According to the Meteorological Department, there is no possibility of thunderstorms or rainfall until 17 July. Light clouds may appear during the day, but humid conditions and rising temperatures are expected to cause discomfort. Bright sunshine in Bareilly; rain alert remains in place The weather remained clear in Bareilly on Sunday morning, with bright sunshine. The maximum temperature is expected to reach 36°C, while the minimum is likely to remain around 29°C. Winds are blowing at a speed of 18 kmph. Weather scientists have issued a yellow alert for rain during the day. Clouds over Varanasi; monsoon likely to remain weak for a few days The weather remained clear in Varanasi on Sunday morning, although light clouds were visible. The temperature was recorded at 36°C, while winds were blowing at 16 kmph. Weather scientist Manoj Srivastava said the monsoon is likely to remain weak for the next few days. Light clouds will continue, but as the day progresses, strong sunshine and humid conditions are expected to trouble residents.

stories.title: Shankaracharya calls Ram Mandir 'BJP-RSS office':Police to seek Tinnu's remand; 3 held, including SP leader over posters
stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand on Sunday said, “The Ram Mandir is not truly a Ram Mandir yet; it is an office of the RSS and the BJP. I will visit only when it actually becomes a Ram Mandir.” He added, “The Ram Mandir Trust was formed by the government. The SIT was also constituted by the government. The same people are the thief and the police—what kind of justice can be expected?” The Shankaracharya is currently on an 81-day yatra demanding that the cow be declared the “Rashtra Mata” (Mother of the Nation). As part of the campaign, he reached Rae Bareli at around 8:30 am on Sunday. Meanwhile, police may take the two accused, Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu and Subhash Srivastava, into custody for questioning. Both are scheduled to be produced before a Faizabad court on Monday, where police are expected to seek a seven-day remand. The investigation revealed that Tinnu Yadav had one of the keys to all 54 donation boxes in the Ram Mandir. In Gorakhpur, police on Saturday evening arrested three people, including Samajwadi Party leader Arvind Shukla, for allegedly putting up posters over the donation theft case. The posters, put up on Friday night, read: “Ram naam japna, shraddhaluon dwara chadhaya daan apna. Ramchandra keh gaye Siya se, aisa Kalyug aayega, chor karega mandir mein chori, chowkidar dekhta reh jayega.” (Chant Lord Ram’s name, and the devotees’ donations become your own. As Lord Ram told Sita, such a Kalyug would come when thieves would steal from the temple while the watchman kept watching) Read the Live blog to know about the latest updates

Husband bites wife’s nose for wanting to visit maternal home:Her mother cuts sister-in-law’s nose in revenge after attack
stories.summary: A man allegedly bit off his wife’s nose with his teeth in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, after she insisted on visiting her maternal home. A heated argument between the couple turned into a fight, during which the husband attacked her. Angry over the incident, the injured woman called her mother. When her mother reached the in-laws’ house and saw her daughter’s severed nose, she allegedly attacked her 18-year-old sister-in-law and bit off her nose in revenge. The girl suffered serious injuries and was bleeding. Hearing the commotion, neighbours reached the spot and somehow calmed both families. Later, both sides reached the police station and filed complaints. The woman was taken to her maternal home. The incident took place around 4 pm on Saturday in Dhakherwa village of Padua area, around 40 km from the district headquarters. Police said the husband has been identified as Shravan Kashyap, his wife as Preeti, and his sister as Moni. Both women were treated at a private hospital. Complaints have been submitted by both sides and the matter is being investigated. Marriage 4 years ago, maternal home 2 km away Shravan, elder son of Ramlakhan Kashyap, married Preeti (30), daughter of Banwari Lal (35) from Chachrapurwa village, four years ago. The couple has no children. Shravan works in farming. The distance between Preeti’s maternal home and her in-laws’ house is only around 2 km. The family said Preeti wanted to attend her cousin’s wedding at her maternal home, but Shravan refused. An argument broke out between them on Saturday, which escalated. In anger, Shravan allegedly assaulted his wife and cut her nose. In-laws reached maternal home after an hour After being seriously injured, Preeti informed her maternal family over the phone. On receiving the information, her father Banwari Lal, mother Shridevi and other relatives reached her in-laws’ house. Seeing her daughter in pain, Shridevi confronted Shravan and his family. The argument between both families soon turned into a physical fight. During the clash, Shravan’s sister Moni came forward to intervene. Shridevi allegedly grabbed Moni’s face with both hands and bit her nose, leaving her seriously injured. Medical examination of both parties, police engaged in investigation After receiving information about the dispute, police reached the spot and brought the situation under control. The injured women were sent for medical examination. Both sides have filed complaints against each other. Police said further action will be taken based on the medical reports and investigation findings. Station House Officer Mohit Pundir said, “The dispute started between the husband and wife. Later, members of both families became involved. Both sides have submitted complaints for registration of an FIR. Further action will be taken after investigation.”

stories.title: UP to provide life insurance for livestock:Government to pay 85% premium, financial aid on death or disability; know how to apply
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has approved the ‘Mukhyamantri Risk Management and Livestock Insurance Scheme’ under which more than 2.28 lakh animals will be insured in the state. A budget of ₹60 crore has been allocated for the scheme. The government will bear 85% of the insurance premium, while livestock owners will have to pay the remaining 15%. The scheme will be implemented in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. How to apply for insurance To avail the benefits of the scheme, livestock owners will have to apply at their nearest government veterinary hospital. After the application, the animal will undergo a medical check-up and a 12-digit insurance tag will be attached to its ear. The insurance will become valid only after the tag is installed. An official associated with the scheme said that the government order (GO) may be issued this week. After this, the action plan will be implemented and formal procedures, including selection of the insurance company and appointment of workers, will begin. Applications for the scheme are expected to start between August and September. Who will benefit from the scheme? Livestock and Dairy Development Minister Dharampal Singh said the scheme will benefit small and marginal farmers, landless livestock owners and people running dairy farms. Once a claim is approved after the death of an insured animal, the insurance amount will be directly transferred to the beneficiary’s bank account. If an animal becomes permanently disabled, the insurance company will pay up to 75% of the insured amount. Priority will be given to animals covered under the government’s animal husbandry and dairy schemes. Treatment expenses will not be covered This is a life insurance scheme and not health insurance. This means the cost of treatment of animals will not be covered. Financial assistance will only be provided in case of death or permanent disability of the insured animal. Beneficiaries divided into two categories In the financial year 2026-27, a total of 2,28,350 animals will be insured. Of these, 1,86,800 animals will be covered under the general category for livestock owners, while 41,550 animals will be insured for livestock owners belonging to Scheduled Castes. The Uttar Pradesh government will pay 85% of the insurance premium, while the remaining 15% will have to be paid by the beneficiaries. Scheme to be implemented in all 75 districts Uttar Pradesh currently has around 7,500 cow protection centres, where nearly 13.50 lakh stray cows are being taken care of. The government spends around ₹8 crore every day on these centres. Under the Uttar Pradesh Fodder Policy, green fodder is also being grown on village community and forest department land and supplied to cow shelters. Answers to 5 Important Questions for Cattle Farmers How will compensation be received? If an insured animal dies, the owner will have to inform the veterinary hospital or insurance company within 24 hours. After this, a government veterinarian will conduct a post-mortem examination. For making a claim, the livestock owner must submit a photograph with the dead animal in which the insurance tag on the animal’s ear and its number are clearly visible. After submitting the required documents, the compensation amount will be transferred to the bank account within 30 days. What happens if an animal is not insured? If an animal is not insured and dies due to illness, lightning or an accident, the livestock owner will have to bear the entire loss. Under this scheme, owners can provide protection to their animals by paying only 15% of the premium. What if the insurance tag falls off or gets lost? No claim will be paid unless the insurance tag is present on the animal’s ear at the time of claim. If the tag breaks or falls off, the owner must immediately get a new tag installed through a government veterinarian and update the records. Otherwise, the claim may get delayed. Will insurance continue if an insured animal is sold? No. The old insurance policy will end once the animal is sold. If the new buyer also falls under the eligible category (small or marginal farmer), they will have to get the policy transferred to their name through the veterinary officer. Without transferring the policy, the new owner will not be eligible for the claim. Can calves of cows and buffaloes be insured? Under this scheme, only milch animals or large animals that are at least 2 to 3 years old will be insured. Newborn or very young animals will not be covered. Among small animals, only adult sheep, goats and pigs are included under the scheme.

stories.title: No bikes on Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway:AI cameras to detect crashes, toll up to 3x; India's first barrier-free highway
stories.summary: Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway is ready and will be inaugurated on July 13 by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari, and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. It will open to the public on July 14. The 63-km expressway is expected to cut travel time between Lucknow and Kanpur from the current 2.5–3 hours to just 45 minutes, according to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). However, commuters will have to pay significantly higher tolls. A car journey between the two cities will now cost ₹275, compared with ₹95 on the existing route. Two-wheelers will not be allowed on the expressway. It will also become India's first barrier-free expressway, with Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras and FASTag readers installed 500 metres before toll plazas to deduct tolls without requiring vehicles to stop. In case of an accident, AI-enabled cameras will instantly alert the NHAI control room. Bhaskar visited the expressway and spoke to residents of Lucknow and Kanpur to understand what the new corridor means for commuters. Here's the full ground report. See 2 pictures of the Expressway Benefits of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway Elevated stretch to ease city traffic Around 18 km of the expressway is elevated, helping motorists avoid traffic bottlenecks near Amausi, Sarojininagar, and NH-27. The elevated section extends up to the old Scooters India campus, allowing vehicles to move without interruptions. Direct connectivity to the Outer Ring Road The expressway has been linked to the Lucknow Outer Ring Road, enabling vehicles coming from Kanpur to head directly towards Rae Bareli, Sitapur, Hardoi, and Sultanpur without entering the city. Service lanes have also been built for smooth entry and exit to the Ring Road. Several villages in Unnao to benefit From Amausi to Darogakhera, the expressway runs alongside the National Highway. Beyond Bani, it branches off into a new greenfield corridor. The route passes through several villages in Unnao district and extends up to Amarsas, an area that previously lacked a major road connection. Interchanges on the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway High-voltage power line was the biggest construction challenge According to NHAI officials, the most difficult stretch to build was near Gauri Chauraha in Banthra, Lucknow, where a 132-kV high-voltage transmission line passed through the alignment. To overcome the challenge, engineers installed special monopole structures to shift the power line. Although the relocation faced initial technical hurdles, construction on this section was completed once the line was successfully moved. What Lucknow and Kanpur residents say 'The toll is beyond the reach of common people' Rahul, a resident near Banthra, said the expressway would be a major benefit for people who frequently travel to Kanpur. Earlier, the journey took 2 to 2.5 hours, while the new expressway is expected to reduce travel time to just 45 minutes. However, he criticised the steep toll charges, saying the earlier toll was reasonable but the new ₹275 fee would put an unnecessary burden on ordinary commuters. He said the government should reconsider the revised toll rates. 'The distance between villages and cities has reduced, but the financial burden has increased' Local resident Amit Kumar said the expressway would make travel to Kanpur and Lucknow much easier for people living in rural areas. It would save time and improve connectivity. However, he believes the current toll rates are beyond the budget of ordinary commuters. He added that the higher toll would be especially burdensome for families making frequent trips during weddings and other social occasions. 'The higher toll is partly justified by savings in time and fuel' Rishabh Jaiswal, a Kanpur resident who travels to Lucknow once or twice a month, said the journey currently takes 2 to 2.5 hours because of traffic. Once the expressway opens, travel time is expected to come down to 50–60 minutes. He said that although the ₹275 toll is high, the savings in travel time and fuel could offset the additional cost. He also suggested that commuters would benefit if the existing National Highway FASTag or toll pass could be made valid on the new expressway. 'An annual pass for frequent travellers would provide relief' Rajesh Pathak, another resident of Kanpur, said the new expressway would make his regular commute much easier, reducing a 2.5–3-hour journey to less than an hour. He believes the project will significantly improve connectivity between Lucknow and Kanpur. He urged the government to either reduce toll charges or introduce an annual pass for frequent users to make the expressway more affordable for regular commuters.

stories.title: Situation worsens in Ayodhya after Ram Mandir donation case surfaces:Number of devotees drops severely, hotel occupancy down to 25%
stories.summary: Faith remains strong in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, but locals of the iconic city say that the atmosphere has changed since allegations of Ram Mandir donation theft surfaced. The situation had worsened after severe allegations of donation theft were imposed on people linked to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust surfaced. Locals blame Ram Mandir donation theft case for worsening situation? At 10 am, devotees continue to queue through the Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Gate on Rampath to offer prayers to Ram Lalla. A sandalwood and garland seller on Rampath said the number of devotees has dropped to a mere 25% of when compared to the footfall prior to theft allegations. Similarly, a prasad vendor said he earlier used to earn ₹4,000–5,000 a day, but now struggles to make ₹1,000. Surya Prakash, who sells flowers and garlands at Naya Ghat, said his daily earnings have fallen from ₹1,000–1,500 to around ₹500. An E-rickshaw driver, Ajay, said he can no longer cover even his operating costs for his vehicle. At breakfast time, all tables at a popular restaurant on Rampath remain empty. A manager of one such restaurant said that business has remained weak for the past 10 days. He blamed the worsening situation on the donation theft controversy, the reopening of schools, and monsoon rains. However, most shopkeepers, hotel owners, and auto and e-rickshaw drivers believe the controversy is the main reason for the fall in pilgrims. What do the devotees say? According to locals, daily footfall has dropped from 100,000–150,000 devotees to around 60,000–70,000. Sumit, a visitor from Gujarat, said his first visit required a four-hour wait for darshan, while this time it took only one hour. Arun Agrawal, spokesperson for the Ayodhya Hotels Association, said occupancy in mid-segment hotels has fallen to 25%. Around 100 new hotels are under construction around Ayodhya, and if religious tourism does not recover soon, investments could be severely affected. A travel agency owner added that most current visitors are from nearby areas and do not require hotels or taxis. Saints remain divided over the case Mahant Acharya Mithileshanandini Sharan of Siddhapeeth Shri Hanumat Niwas said the issue is an administrative failure, not the institution's, and alleged attempts are being made to weaken public faith. He said the truth will soon emerge. Mahant Kamal Nayan Das, successor of Maniram Das Chhawani, said only a few lower-level employees were at fault and action has already been taken. He said Trust General Secretary Champat Rai was not responsible. Mahant Dharmdas of Hanumangarhi demanded that the Trust be dissolved and replaced with a new body of Ayodhya saints. He said they would approach the Supreme Court if necessary. Mahant Vivek Achari of Dantdhavan Kund Temple called for Shankaracharyas and Peethadheeshwars to be included in the Trust. Mahant Janmejaya Sharan demanded greater representation for Ayodhya's saints in the Trust. UP elections nine months away The controversy has grown beyond the alleged donation theft and investigation. Since the Ram Temple has long been a key ideological symbol for the BJP and RSS, allegations against the Trust have given the Opposition a major political issue ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, due in about nine months. After initially remaining silent, the BJP and RSS have launched a damage-control campaign. Party workers and volunteers are telling people that the SIT probe is underway, action has been taken against those responsible, and major reforms are being introduced in the Trust. Speculation about early Assembly elections had grown after the West Bengal results and the census process, but following the Trust controversy, the BJP is reportedly not in favour of advancing polls, fearing political damage if elections are held before the issue subsides. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has assured strict action against those found guilty. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya challenged Akhilesh Yadav to clarify his stand on the Mathura Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi issue. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav said the matter concerns public faith, demanded a fair investigation without any cover-up, and said his party would raise the issue during Parliament's Monsoon Session.

stories.title: BJP may deny tickets to 40% of UP MLAs:Poor performers likely to be dropped; national president says don't sit idle if denied a ticket
stories.summary: 'Even if the ticket is cut, don't sit at home, have to make the party win...' That was the message BJP national president Nitin Navin delivered during his Uttar Pradesh visit, signalling that only candidates with strong winnability will be fielded in the next Assembly election. Around 40% of sitting MLAs with poor public image or weak organisational connect could lose their tickets. Nitin Navin spent 36 hours in Lucknow on 4–5 July, holding meetings with the government, the party organisation and RSS functionaries to assess the political situation. His focus remained on 240 Assembly constituencies where BJP MPs had performed poorly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections despite having BJP MLAs. The national president wants candidates capable of winning these seats. A BJP organisation functionary said the central leadership has already conducted surveys across Uttar Pradesh, which predict defeat for several sitting MLAs. Based on these findings, the national president has identified six categories that will determine candidature: The party is also reviewing MLAs who retained their seats by very narrow margins in the 2022 Assembly election, with some winning by just 200 to 300 votes. How BJP changed candidates in previous elections Teacher/Graduate MLC Elections- How to Win Lost Seats Will give opportunity to new faces on 6 seats Preparations are underway for elections to 11 Teachers' and Graduates' constituency seats in the Legislative Council. BJP has announced candidates for five seats, all of whom had won in the 2020 elections. The party has withheld its candidate for the Meerut Graduates' seat, which was won by BJP's Dinesh Kumar Goyal. Of the remaining six seats, three are held by the Samajwadi Party and two by Independents. At a BJP core group meeting, it was agreed in principle that candidates for these seats would be selected through two approaches: leaders who won previously and remain in touch with the party, and fresh winnable faces from within the organisation. Polling dates for these 11 Legislative Council seats are yet to be announced. The elections are scheduled for December 2026. After approval from the Central Election Committee, BJP has declared candidates for five seats. The party has also reached an in-principle agreement to replace candidates or field new faces on six seats. BJP had lost both seats in Varanasi in the previous election. It did not field a candidate for the Gorakhpur–Faizabad Teachers' constituency, where Independent candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi won. Discussions are underway to field him as the BJP candidate this time. National President Identified 3 Major Weaknesses 1. Restore deleted voters in ministers' and MLAs' constituencies Nitin Navin expressed concern over the removal of nearly 20.4 million names during Uttar Pradesh's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He was informed that thousands of voters had been deleted even from constituencies represented by ministers and MLAs. He advised leaders to review the lists and ensure that names deleted by mistake are restored. 2. Avoid public comments on Ram Temple donation theft At a meeting with ministers and MLAs at Lucknow's Taj Hotel, Nitin Navin described the alleged Ram Temple donation theft as a serious mistake that had hurt public faith. He instructed party leaders not to make public statements on the sensitive issue, saying it had already provided the Opposition with a political issue. During the core group meeting, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the SIT had submitted its preliminary findings and that a detailed report would be available after 15 July, following which legal action would be taken against those found guilty. 3. Find a lasting solution to the UGC regulations issue The BJP is also working on a permanent solution to the controversy surrounding the new UGC regulations. While members of the upper castes have expressed dissatisfaction with the rules, OBC and Dalit groups are unhappy because of the Supreme Court's stay on certain provisions. During a separate meeting with RSS office-bearers at the Vishva Samvad Kendra, the RSS also acknowledged that both the Ram Temple donation theft issue and the UGC controversy had created public dissatisfaction that could affect the party electorally. Nitin Navin discussed these issues separately with ministers, MLAs and organisational office-bearers. Advised on lack of coordination The BJP recently announced its new Uttar Pradesh state team under state president Pankaj Chaudhary, appointing 52 office-bearers, including 19 vice-presidents, eight general secretaries, 19 secretaries and six regional presidents. During the meetings attended by the national president, a lack of coordination among these office-bearers became evident. Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh advised them to address these shortcomings well before the Assembly elections. Nitin Navin asked organisational office-bearers two key questions: The meeting also decided that Uttar Pradesh's three-tier panchayat elections would be held only after the Assembly elections. Bypolls to the Dudhi, Ghosi and Faridpur Assembly seats will also be conducted along with the main Assembly election. Party leaders have been instructed to focus all their efforts on the Assembly polls.

stories.title: Minister Rajbhar targets Akhilesh Yadav:'He divorced us'; says SP and Congress have lost relevance
stories.summary: In Ballia, Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said that Akhilesh Yadav has divorced him. That's why whenever he faces him, he gets angry. Rajbhar claimed that both the SP and Congress parties are duds. Rajbhar was speaking at BJP's Jan Samvad program on Saturday evening at 6:30 pm. He said that in 2017, SP won 47 seats. But in the 2027 assembly elections, winning even 27 seats would be a big achievement for them. The program was organised at Bhikha Bhagat Pokhra complex. Power can be inherited, not wisdom Om Prakash Rajbhar said that he has prepared many wrestlers in politics. Comparing himself to the mythological character Bali, he said- Just as half the strength of opponents would vanish when Bali appeared before them, similarly, seeing him gives opponents a 100-degree fever. Power can be inherited, but not wisdom. SP leaders oppose BJP during the day, while at night they meet Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He also has photos related to this. Rajbhar also mentioned the letter written by Ramgopal Yadav to Home Minister Amit Shah during this time. Overconfidence about political future Referring to the Women's Reservation Bill, Rajbhar said that PM Modi brought a law to give 33 percent reservation to women in Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha. But Samajwadi Party, Congress, TMC, and Shiv Sena opposed it. Rajbhar claimed that parties opposing women's reservation have weakened. During the upcoming monsoon session, a split will also be seen in the Samajwadi Party. He said that SP should not be overconfident about its political future. Rajbhar also mentioned his political struggle. He said that when he started the campaign to bring forward the honor and history of Maharaja Suheldev on October 27, 2002, he faced strong opposition. The minister said that history and heritage are the greatest strength of any society. Without history, no society or leadership can last long. SP workers protested before Om Prakash Rajbhar's proposed public meeting in Ratsar, Phephna assembly constituency. Outside the party office on the Gadwar-Phephna road, SP workers showed black flags and raised slogans against the minister. They objected to the statement made regarding SP MP Sanatan Pandey. In view of the apprehension of protest, additional police force was deployed. Meanwhile, due to security reasons, the minister Rajbhar's travel route was also changed. Officials said that surveillance has been increased throughout the area to maintain law and order.

stories.title: Lovers jump into river holding hands:Youth texts uncle, 'I'm going to die, my bullet is parked on the bridge'
stories.summary: A couple allegedly jumped into the Ramganga River holding hands from a bridge in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday afternoon. They had arrived at around 2:30 pm on a Bullet motorcycle, parked it by the roadside, spoke for a while and then leapt into the river together. Before jumping, the young man sent a message to his uncle saying, ‘Uncle, I am going to die. The bike is parked on the Ramganga bridge. Come with the other key.’ By the time his family reached the bridge, both had already jumped. Katghar Police, assisted by local divers, are searching for the pair, but neither has been found so far. See 3 pictures Before dying, he messaged his uncle According to the police, the youth was identified as Tushar (20), son of Nanhe. He was a resident of Suraj Nagar, Pital Basti, under the Katghar police station area. Tushar's house is about 4 km away from the incident site. Tushar's uncle, Sudhir Goswami, said that Tushar worked as a salesman at a clothing shop in Budh Bazaar in the city. As usual, he had gone from home to the shop on Saturday morning. While leaving home, Tushar had asked me for ₹100 in the morning. I had given them to him. After that, around 12 noon, he messaged me on my mobile saying that I am going to jump into Ramganga, I will take my own life. After receiving the message, family members who arrived at the scene found Tushar's Bullet motorcycle parked. Seeing the Bullet, the family members were distraught and cried inconsolably. The police have taken the Bullet into custody. Left the shop by lying After the incident, the police also gathered information about the events from the cloth shop owner. The shop owner said - Tushar had taken leave from the shop at 12 PM. He had said that he had some very urgent work at home, which is why he was going home. But after leaving the shop, he did not go home. Man was troubled by family restrictions It is being reported that Tushar had an affair with a minor girl from the neighborhood. The girl is also missing from her home. It is being said that both, troubled by family restrictions, jumped into the river with the intention of suicide. However, neither the family nor the police have confirmed this yet. It is believed to be the same girl who jumped into the river with Tushar. Currently, the police are investigating this. The police and a team of divers are engaged in the search for both. Diver Mohammad Wasim said- We received information from the police that a young man had jumped into the river from the bypass bridge. When we arrived here, we found that both the young man and the young woman had jumped into the Ramganga. Our team searched extensively. Many divers also went swimming to search, but the river has a lot of water and is deep. The water level is also rising rapidly. Therefore, there is no trace of either of them yet. Our diving team from the police, PRV, and Jama Masjid is engaged in the search. The boy's age is being told as 20 to 22 years. His family members are also present at the spot. Blood was also found near the bike SP City Ranvijay Singh, who arrived at the spot, said, On Saturday, a young man and a young woman jumped from the Ramganga bridge. Police teams are continuously engaged in their search with the help of local divers and the flood unit. A Bullet bike was found parked on the same bridge from where both of them jumped. It belongs to a boy named Tushar. Blood was also found near the bike and on the edge of the bridge. Currently, the police's first priority is to rescue both of them. Our teams are continuously working on this.

stories.title: BJP to sideline inactive booth presidents:Workers to verify SIR voter lists door-to-door; Pankaj Chaudhary says polls will be held on time
stories.summary: The BJP has stepped up preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections by launching an intensive door-to-door voter list verification campaign. Party workers will visit households with the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list to verify voter details and ensure that every citizen aligned with the party's ideology is included on the electoral roll. The party is also identifying booth presidents who have been negligent in their duties. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary at the party's state headquarters in Lucknow on Saturday. General Secretary's Mantra - 'If the voter list work improves, we've climbed the first step to victory' In the meeting, General Secretary (Organisation) Dharampal Singh presented the election roadmap and said, If we successfully complete the verification of the voter list and the work of adding new names, then understand that we have climbed the first step of the assembly elections. He gave several guidelines to strengthen the organisation Non-active booth presidents will be removed: Verification of presidents will be done at each booth. New faces will get a chance in place of booth presidents who are not active. After this, their conferences will be held at the district level. Leaders to stay for 7 to 10 days: State office bearers will no longer be allowed to rest. They will have to stay in districts for 7 to 10 days every month. Similarly, district presidents will camp in mandals and mandal teams will camp at booths. In the meeting, State President Pankaj Chaudhary said, There will be no premature elections in Uttar Pradesh. There are still about eight months left for the assembly elections, so everyone should get fully prepared. 'Workers should counter opposition's lies with facts' Advising the workers, the State President said, The opposition is constantly trying to create an atmosphere of lies, confusion, and misinformation. In such a situation, it is the responsibility of BJP workers to go among the public and on social media and counter this narrative of the opposition based on facts. Seniors to be given command, advised to remain accessible at the grassroots level Chaudhary said - Learn from the experience of senior workers Pankaj Chaudhary said that the experience of old senior workers should be utilised in election preparations or upcoming campaigns, and they should be given responsibility. Office bearers have been strictly instructed to maintain a very simple demeanor during their interactions with the public and workers. State General Secretary Sanjay Rai, Abhijat Mishra, Geeta Shakya, Shankar Lodhi, State Vice Presidents Neeraj Singh, Archana Pandey, State Ministers Rajni Pandey, Rahul Valmiki, Sahajanand Rai, Basant Tyagi, Vijay Shivhare, and Rohit Mishra, State President of Yuva Morcha, along with several other key office bearers, were present at the meeting. In the coming days, BJP will organise these programs on a large scale, not just for formality, but to increase public trust:

stories.title: UP Congress in-charge alleges poor-quality milk served on Vande Bharat:Says fare is premium but milk is 'chemical-like', complains to Rail Minister
stories.summary: The Vande Bharat Express' premium service has come under scrutiny after Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam alleged that poor-quality milk was served during his journey on Train No. 22470 from Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi to Jhansi on Saturday. Gautam shared videos of the milk on social media, claiming its quality was substandard. The Uttar Pradesh Congress also posted the videos, saying, 'The fare is premium, but the milk is chemical-like.' Former Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee president Brijlal Khabri was travelling with Gautam at the time. Made video himself, complained to Railway Minister and IRCTC Rajendra Pal Gautam and Brijlal Khabri were traveling with two other people on Saturday by Vande Bharat Express (22470). The four leaders were in coach E2 (seat numbers 1, 2, 3, 4) of the train. They were given milk on the train. Seeing the poor quality of the milk, Rajendra Pal Gautam himself made a video of it. Then, to expose this mischief with the health of passengers, he posted it on social media. In addition, he lodged a written complaint about this serious matter by tagging the Railway Minister and IRCTC on social media through PNR number 2955075897. Congress leader said - Why is the government so kind to vendors? Congress leaders have raised serious questions about the functioning of the railways. They said that such milk is being served to VIPs like the UP Congress in-charge on expensive trains like Vande Bharat. This clearly shows what must be happening to common passengers? The condition of passengers traveling in ordinary trains must be even worse than this. They asked why the Indian Railways and the central government, which empty the pockets of the public in the name of fare, are so kind to these vendors? Demand for high-level investigation and strict action Congress demanded a high-level investigation into the entire matter and lab testing of the milk sample. The party says that serving such 'chemical' to passengers in the name of Vande Bharat is extremely shameful. Strict legal action should be taken against the responsible vendor and company. Leaders gone to attend Congress's worker dialogue program Actually, UP Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam is touring the entire state. In this sequence, he reached Jhansi on Saturday. Here too, there was a Congress worker interaction program. Office bearers and workers of the city and district Congress committee participated in it. His effort is that in the next 3 months, the district organisation, from booth level to district level, should become fully active in every district. Along with this, he is also busy preparing the Congress's election manifesto by discussing with common people. He claims that Congress will resolve the seat-sharing issue by September. After this, the candidate selection process will begin. UP Congress in-charge on tour till 14 July Rajendra Pal will stay in Jhansi tonight. On 12 July, he will meet BIDA-affected farmers in Babina. After this, he will go to Mahoba. There, he will interact with Congress leaders from Hamirpur and Mahoba. Then in the evening, he will reach Banda. He will rest for the night in Chitrakoot. On 13 July, he will interact with officials from Chitrakoot, then Prayagraj, Kaushambi, and Fatehpur districts. In Prayagraj, he will hold a meeting with lawyers through the 'Coffee with Barrister' program. On 14 July, he will participate in the 'Students' Echo' program. Then he will come to Pratapgarh and from there to Lucknow.

stories.title: UP's first non-government AI lab opens in Varanasi:Students to receive advanced technical education
stories.summary: A state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotics Lab was inaugurated at 4 pm on Saturday at PM Shri Rajkiya Queens Inter College in Varanasi. Organisers said it is the first AI and Robotics lab to be set up in a government school in Uttar Pradesh without any government financial assistance, aiming to equip students with practical skills in emerging technologies. The lab was developed under the guidance of former principal Sumeet Kumar Srivastava and the Queens College Alumni Association, led by Prof. Dharmendra Singh, Director of IIIT Vadodara, with support from PHN Technology. Although the facility was completed around six months ago, it was formally inaugurated on Saturday. Speaking at the event, Prof. Singh said the lab would help students build expertise in AI and robotics while encouraging innovation, start-ups and entrepreneurship. Students to get state-of-the-art facilities in the lab Pradeep H. Narayankar, representative of PHN Technology, said that their organization has been working for a long time to promote technical education. He informed that this lab has been equipped with state-of-the-art resources and modern equipment, and its quality is equivalent to that of any IIT laboratory. According to him, new opportunities for employment and self-employment will open up for students receiving training here. Provision to also be made for trained instructors Prof. Pradeep Kumar Mishra, President of Queen's College Alumni Association, called it a historic day in the history of the school and said that this lab will provide a new direction to the technical future of the students. He informed that trained instructors will also be arranged for the effective operation of the lab, so that students can receive regular and quality training. Professor Manoj Srivastava of BHU also participated in the program.

stories.title: Youth in Gorakhpur to receive folk music training:Free 10-day workshop begins on 12 July; registration free
stories.summary: A 10-day workshop on traditional folk songs will be organised by Sharda Sangeetalaya of Gorakhpur in collaboration with the Culture Department, Uttar Pradesh. It will start on 12 July at 4 pm and will continue till 21 July. This event will be held at S.S. Academy, located opposite AD Mall. During this, the new generation will be given practical training in many traditional folk songs like Kajri, Sohar, wedding songs, Jhumar, Chaita, Nirgun. Registration for participants will be free. People of all ages can participate. Folk songs are the cultural identity of folk life - Dr. Rakesh Dr. Rakesh Srivastava, the workshop trainer and folk singer, said that folk songs are the cultural identity of Indian folk life. This workshop is being organised with the aim of preserving, promoting them, and connecting the new generation with their folk traditions. He informed that practical training of various traditional folk songs, including Kajri, Sohar, wedding songs, Jhumar, Chaita, Nirgun will be given in the workshop. Men and women of all age groups can participate in it for free. Interested people can get their free registration done by attending the workshop venue on 12 July at 4 pm. Dr. Srivastava has appealed to the music lovers and youth of the district to participate in large numbers and make this cultural campaign a success.

stories.title: Case registered against doctor couple over fake trust deed:Court orders FIR for opening RBL Bank accounts
stories.summary: Malay Mohan, Branch Manager of RBL Bank's Indiranagar branch in Lucknow, has accused a doctor couple of opening bank accounts through a fake trust deed, irregularities in financial transactions, and threatening to kill him. The manager complained to the police, but when no action was taken, he sought help from the court. Following this, a case was registered on the court's order. Branch Manager Mayal Mohan stated in his complaint to the police that in 2022, accounts were opened in the Indiranagar branch of RBL Bank in the names of Hind Charitable Trust's institutions, Hind Institute of Medical Sciences, Safedabad (Barabanki), and Hind Institute of Medical Sciences, Ataria (Sitapur). While opening the accounts, Dr. Amod Kumar Sachan and his wife, Richa Mishra, submitted the trust deed and other KYC documents, identifying themselves as authorized representatives of the trust. Claim of trust deed being fake in investigation The bank manager alleges that after receiving information about the embezzlement case registered at Kaiserbagh police station in March 2026, the police instructed to stop the operation of the trust's accounts. Following this, the bank made all accounts 'no-debit'. Later, when the original deed of the trust was verified, it was found that the trust deed submitted to the bank was forged. The original trust deed had seven trustees, whereas the document submitted to the bank showed only Dr. Amod Kumar Sachan and Richa Mishra as trustees. Allegation of death threat over phone Malay Mohan states that Dr. Amod Kumar Sachan, angered by the freezing of accounts, called on the night of March 17 and pressured him to immediately reactivate the accounts. When the bank expressed its inability, he used abusive language and threatened to kill him and his family, not let him live in Lucknow, and prevent him from working. The bank manager also has a recording of the conversation as evidence. Allegation of police inaction Malay Mohan says that he sent a written complaint to Ghazipur police station and later to the Police Commissioner, but no FIR was registered. After this, he filed a petition in court demanding registration of a case against Dr. Amod Kumar Sachan and Richa Mishra under relevant sections including fraud, forgery, and intimidation. On whose order, the case was registered. Information about scam up to 94 crores Manvendra Singh, son of Hind Institute of Medical Sciences Founder Trustee Brij Kishore Singh, said that when they came to know that there was some irregularity in the bank accounts. On investigating at the bank, it was found that a fake deed was prepared by forging their original deed. In which only Dr. Amod Kumar Sachan and Richa Mishra are present, and through them, all bank operations are being conducted. In this way, a lot of college money has been spent on irrelevant and personal things. The police have informed the court in writing that fraud up to 94 crores has been detected. But this case could be worth more than 600 crores. No contact has been made since the fraud. They just claim that the college is theirs. Kaiserbagh police have collected all the evidence. Now it is unknown why there is a delay in action. Regarding the matter, the Station House Officer of Ghazipur says that a case has been registered. Action will be taken based on the evidence.

stories.title: Tourism department launches new Kashi package for visitors:Tourists can explore temples with a guide for ₹2,200
stories.summary: For devotees and tourists visiting Kashi, the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department has launched special Heritage Walk packages with the aim of offering a tour of the city's major religious and cultural sites in a short time and at an affordable cost. Through these packages, tourists will be able to experience the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, prominent ghats, ancient temples, Ganga Aarti, and Banarasi cuisine in approximately five hours. Tourism department launches website Dinesh Kumar, Joint Director of the Tourism Department, stated, The objective of these packages is to introduce tourists visiting for a short duration to the spiritual, cultural, and historical heritage of Kashi. The packages are being promoted at various locations, including Cantt Railway Station, Airport, Ganga Ghats, and Kashi Vishwanath Dham. Interested tourists can book online by visiting the department's website www.darshan-kashi-gov.in or by scanning the designated QR code. Tourism department has released 3 packages The Tourism Department has prepared three special packages. The Divya Kashi Heritage Walk is priced at 2,200 rupees per person. It includes Mangala Aarti, darshan at Kashi Vishwanath Temple, visits to several major religious sites including Maa Annapurna, Vishalakshi, Pashupatinath, Manikarnika Ghat, Rudraksha mala, prasad, guide, and refreshments. The second Assi Kashi Heritage Walk package is ₹2,500 per person. It will include 'Subah-e-Banaras' at Assi Ghat with Mangala Aarti, travel by boat or e-bus, darshan at major temples, a taste of Banarasi tea and kachori, and guide facilities. The third is the Old Kashi Heritage Walk evening package, priced at ₹2,499 per person. It includes facilities such as Man Mandir Observatory, prominent temples, Ganga Aarti at Lalita Ghat, VIP darshan at Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Banarasi Chaat experience, and a guide and prasad.

stories.title: 7-year-old girl gang-raped and murdered:Abducted while playing outside home; semi-naked body found in mall; FIR against 3
stories.summary: A 7-year-old girl was gang-raped and then murdered in Ghaziabad on Friday. Around 1 am, her body was found semi-naked and covered in blood in the basement of an under-construction mall. The girl's head was crushed, and there were also injury marks on her throat. According to family members, the girl was playing outside her home around 7 pm. After this, she suddenly went missing. Despite extensive searching, when she couldn't be found, the police were informed late at night. Police scanned the footage from nearby CCTV cameras, in which three youths were seen taking the girl towards the basement of the under-construction building. Police searched the basement, where the girl's body was recovered. She was unclothed. The incident occurred in the Nandgram police station area, 7 kilometers away from the district headquarters. Police have registered a case of gang-rape and kidnapping against three accused. Police have taken two people into custody and are interrogating them. Complete details According to the police, on Friday night around 10 pm, the child's family reached Nandgram police station. They stated that they are residents of Bihar and work as laborers in the under-construction mall. Their family lives within the mall premises. The family told the police that around 7 pm, their daughter was playing outside the house. After that, she suddenly disappeared. Despite extensive searching, she could not be found, after which the police were informed. Around 1 am late at night, information was received on Dial-112 about a body found in the basement. Clue found from CCTV footage According to the family, the police searched the CCTV footage from cameras installed around the mall. In one camera, three youths were seen taking the girl towards the basement. After this, the basement was searched, where the girl's body was found. The family says that the girl's body had no clothes on. Her head was crushed, there were scratch marks on her throat, and blood was flowing from her body. After this, they filed a complaint against three accused, on which the police registered a case. Mother said - When daughter's body was found, she had no clothes on The girl's mother said, My daughter was 7 years old. She was missing since Friday evening. Her body was found at night. When the body was found, she had no clothes on. Three people did wrong to her. DCP inspected the crime scene As soon as information about the incident was received, senior officials were informed. A short while later, DCP City Dhaval Jaiswal reached the spot along with officials. Forensic and dog squad teams were also called. Officials took information about the incident from the family members and inspected the crime scene. Accused said - Raped under the influence of intoxication On the instructions of the DCP, the police started searching for the accused. At night, two accused were taken into custody some distance from the mall. While one of their accomplices is absconding. During interrogation, the accused told that all three of them are laborers and work in another nearby building. They had sat together and consumed alcohol. After that, they took the girl to the basement and raped her. Police said - Accused confessed to the crime DCP City Dhaval Jaiswal stated, The gangrape of the girl has been confirmed. Based on the complaint of the family, an FIR has been registered against three accused. Of these, two accused have been taken into custody, while the search for the third is ongoing. According to the police, the accused have confessed to their crime during interrogation. Further interrogation is currently underway.

stories.title: Temple crumbles down during bulldozer demolition, 1 killed:Structure built in middle of road, was being removed for widening
stories.summary: A labourer was killed and another injured, after the dome of the 200-year-old Kali Mata Temple suddenly collapsed during a bulldozer demolition in Chandauli, Uttar Pradesh, on Friday night. The accident occurred at around 11 pm in Mughalsarai, while the temple, located in the middle of the road, was being demolished as part of the Mughalsarai–Varanasi road-widening project. Both labourers were standing about 10 feet away holding a rope when the dome collapsed so quickly that they were unable to escape and were buried under the debris. Locals pulled them out after removing the rubble, but 58-year-old Baldev Yadav died, while the other labourer was injured. A video of the incident has also surfaced, and officials halted the demolition work after reaching the site. See 3 pictures- Find out what's visible in the video The video shows Baldev Yadav and another laborer standing, holding a rope, while the bulldozer demolishes the temple. Suddenly, the temple begins to collapse. After the temple's dome collides with the bulldozer, it changes direction and turns towards both labourers. Both try to run, but the dome breaks through the barricading and falls on them. People and policemen present nearby pulled both of them out and took them to the CHC. There, doctors declared Baldev dead, while the other labourer is undergoing treatment. Brother said - Family should get 50 lakh compensation Nathni Yadav, a resident of Jhumri, alleged that he was informed about the incident approximately an hour after his brother Baldev's death. When he reached the spot, no one told him the correct information. After much inquiry, a policeman handed over his brother's mobile phone. He demanded that the family be given a compensation of 50 lakh and Baldev's son be given a job. SDM said - will provide all possible help to the family SDM Rajiv Mohan Saxena said, All possible help would be provided to the family. Currently, the matter is being investigated. The road widening work was awarded to a private company. Baldev had been working for the same company for the last 3 years. The company will also help the family.

stories.title: Yogi asks crowd who wants to act with Ravi Kishan:Attacks oppn, says, 'Those raising questions did nothing when they had power'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took a light-hearted dig at Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan during a public meeting in Kushinagar at around 11:30 am on Friday. Asking the crowd how many had watched Ravi Kishan's films and who wanted to act alongside him, the Chief Minister smiled and said, First, work with MP Vijay Dubey. Then you will also get a chance to work with Ravi Kishan. Attacking the opposition, he said, Today, those who question us about development, I want to ask them, what did they do when they were in power? Those who themselves could do nothing, are today making accusations. Before 2017, the state had neither the intention nor a clear policy, which is why development works remained stalled. The Chief Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for development projects worth approximately ₹525 crore for the Ramkola, Hata, and Kushinagar tehsils of the district. The CM also honored elderly BJP workers, 110-year-old Ramvilas Bhagat and 104-year-old Rampravesh Sahni. Main points of CM Yogi's speech 1. Samajwadi goons used to grab the jobs and land of the poor The Chief Minister said that before 2017, obstacles were created even in the organisation of festivals like Durga Puja, Janmashtami, and Holi. Samajwadi goons used to grab the jobs and land of the poor, but the double-engine government does not tolerate hooliganism at all. Now, if anyone tries to spoil the atmosphere or create mischief during festivals, strict action is taken against them. Now, no curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. 2. Earlier boundary walls of cemeteries were built, now renovation of temples Yogi said that when governments themselves are victims of policy paralysis, how will policies be made? This was the situation in the state before 2017. Referring to the renovation of temples, he said that today temples are being renovated in every assembly constituency. Earlier, boundary walls of cemeteries were built with the money received in the name of temples. But now that doesn't happen. 3. Targeting previous governments while mentioning encephalitis Yogi said that it used to be this season when a large number of children died due to Japanese encephalitis. The governments of that time were insensitive and did not even make adequate arrangements for the treatment of children. Today, we have eradicated encephalitis from its roots. When I see a smile on the faces of these children, I feel that life has become meaningful. 4. Musahar community received respect Yogi said that those who did politics in the name of the poor and deprived sections for years did not give the Musahar community their rights. Today, there is a smile on the faces of the Musahar community, and they have realized that they too are respected citizens of this country. This change has been possible due to the schemes of the double-engine government. 5. Airport operations will commence upon receipt of new aircraft CM Yogi said that due to the Corona pandemic and global war, new aircraft could not be made available on time. Because of this, the operation of Kushinagar Airport could not start at the expected pace. As soon as new aircraft are available, Kushinagar Airport will be developed as a model international airport and will also be connected to Jewar and Ayodhya airports. 6. CM asked - Will you act with Ravi Kishan? The Chief Minister took a dig at Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan, who was present at the event. He said, ‘I welcome Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan ji, who has come at the invitation of Kushinagar MP Vijay Dubey.’ After that, smiling, he asked the public, 'How many people have seen Ravi Kishan's film? Who wants to work with him in a film?' Then he said, ‘First work with our MP Vijay Dubey, after that, you will get a chance with Ravi Kishan too.’ The Chief Minister's remark drew laughter from the public gathering. Ravi Kishan said that Maharaj ji called me, the MP did not bring me Earlier, BJP MP Ravi Kishan, in his Bhojpuri style, said, Clap loudly in Maharaj ji's welcome. This is my first time in Tekuatar. Maharaj ji has brought me here. If the MP says he brought me, he is wrong. Maharaj ji brought me, the MP did not call me. At his words, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and everyone present on the stage were seen smiling and laughing.

stories.title: Akhilesh meets Lalita murder victim's family:Iqra brings them from Meerut; SP chief says, 'Those meant to deliver justice are slapping people'
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met the family of the Meerut Lalita murder case victim at 8:30 am on Saturday. He spoke with Lalita’s family behind closed doors for 1 hour and 15 minutes at his official residence in Delhi. He also handed over a cheque of 2 lakh rupees to them. According to sources, Akhilesh called the family on Friday night, inviting them to Delhi for a meeting. Kairana MP Iqra Hasan reached Delhi with her parents and brother. The grieving family narrated the entire incident to Akhilesh. Akhilesh assured Lalita’s father, saying, The daughter will get justice. Once our government is formed, we will provide a job to one member of the family. He also took a swipe at Meerut SSP Avinash Pandey, stating, The very police officers from whom justice is expected are slapping the public out of injustice and arrogance. The video is tarnishing the image of the UP Police. Sensitive police officers are feeling ashamed because of this before the general public. In fact, the body of Lalita Gautam, a BA student, was found in a sugarcane field on 17 May. Alleging gang-rape and murder, the family members had staged a protest outside the Collectorate. Upon receiving information, SSP Avinash Pandey arrived at the spot. It is alleged that he slapped the protesting individuals. The police then launched a baton charge to disperse the protesters from the area. Akhilesh to raise the matter in assembly According to sources, Akhilesh told the family, The accused Ankush's brother, Ankit, who is in the PAC (Pradeshik Armed Constabulary), has been suspended; we will ensure a case is registered against him too and get him arrested. We will also ensure justice for those who were demanding justice for Lalita Gautam at the Collectorate gate, upon whom the police rained batons, sticks, and slaps. We will make every effort to get the cases dropped against the 13 people who were booked by the police simply for demanding justice. We will raise this entire matter in the House. 'Atrocity of a massive scale' committed against 'Meerut’s daughter' Earlier, Akhilesh wrote on ‘X’, When the one holding the reins is himself unbridled, then what can one expect from the gatekeepers of his court? An atrocity of a massive scale has been committed against 'Meerut’s daughter'. Named accused were booked under weak sections of the law, whereas serious sections were slapped against the protesters.This is the pinnacle of injustice. The PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak) will no longer tolerate this, they will speak up. The truth is, in a state where the chief himself publicly displays indecent behaviour towards women, particularly towards the grieving mother of a young deceased, it is futile to expect anything from his police. The fingers only follow the commands of the brain. Victim's family terrified by Meerut SSP’s attitude Iqra Hasan told Dainik Bhaskar that the victim's family has been terrified since the Meerut SSP’s outburst. She said, Today, we met the SP National President Akhilesh Yadav. The SSP used casteist slurs against the grieving family. The heights of arrogance were crossed. This is the first time an IPS officer has indulged in such hooliganism. Immediate action must be taken against such officers. Sangeet Som meets Lalita Gautam’s family Former MLA Sangeet Som visited Lalita Gautam's family and assured them of all possible assistance. He said, "The daughter will get justice at all costs." He also announced financial assistance to cover the lawyer's fees. He added, 'Wrong has been done to the daughter, so she must get justice.' He reassured the family that the entire state government stands with them, and every possible action will be taken to ensure the harshest punishment for the culprits. The government will strongly plead the case under legal procedures to ensure the accused face the gallows. The victim's family should not face any hindrance in fighting a strong legal battle. To ensure this, he announced financial aid from his end for the lawyer's fees, enabling the family to pursue the case through a competent advocate. Right-wing leader Pinky Chaudhary placed under house arrest The National President of Hindu Raksha Dal, Pinky Chaudhary, who was on his way to meet Lalita Gautam’s family in Meerut, was placed under house arrest by the police at his residence in Ghaziabad. MP Chandrashekhar met family yesterday Prior to this, on 10 July, MP Chandrashekhar Azad met Lalita's family in Meerut. Giving a 7-day ultimatum to the administration, the MP stated, ‘If justice is not delivered, we will launch a protest in Lucknow and raise the matter in the Lok Sabha as well.’ Key facts about student Lalita Gautam murder case 'My supporters should plant one sapling, opponents should plant two' Meanwhile, SSP Avinash Pandey released a video on 10 July, stating, Whatever action has been taken, it has been taken against criminals. We have evidence for everything. Those making personal comments about me will be counselled. I will try to make them understand. However, those trying to disrupt law and order will not be forgiven at all. He concluded with an appeal. He said, I would like to appeal to those who support me to plant a tree during the upcoming plantation festival and avoid littering polythene around them. I would also like to appeal to those who oppose me to plant two trees. Channel your anger for the good of society, rather than speaking about a specific caste or supporting criminals who disrupt law and order.

stories.title: Fighter jets soar over Kashi skies:Pilots on Rafale and Surya Kiran team conduct rehearsals ahead of Air Force Day
stories.summary: On Saturday morning at 10 AM in Varanasi, Indian Air Force fighter jets soared in the skies of Kashi. This included Rafale and Surya Kiran. People in the city were surprised by the high-speed flight of three fighter jets simultaneously. From morning, fighter jets continuously circled over Namo Ghat and the city, taking off from different directions. This happened as part of the rehearsal for the proposed air show at Namo Ghat on the occasion of Air Force Day. Crowds gathered at Namo Ghat to watch the fighter jets fly. See 2 pictures The exercise lasted for two and a half hours. The Air Force's 94th Foundation Day is on October 8. This time, the event will be held in Kashi. As part of this, Rafale and Surya Kiran fighter jets flew here on Saturday. Hearing the loud sound echoing in the sky, people came out of their homes, roofs, balconies, and onto the streets. Many people recorded this scene on their mobile phones and shared it on social media. This activity, which started in the morning, continued till approximately 12:30 PM. During this, fighter jets flew in different formations, circling over Namo Ghat multiple times. Their loud roar could be heard far and wide, filling the entire city with excitement. Tremendous enthusiasm among people Rahul, a devotee present at Ganga Ghat, said, “The simultaneous flight of three fighter jets and their high speed greatly attracted people. People present at the ghat continuously engaged in taking pictures and videos of the aircraft. Many people reached Assi Ghat with their families to enjoy this spectacle. For some time, the entire ghat became a witness to this practice flight of the Air Force.” Tight security at Namo Ghat since morning Along with the flight of fighter jets, the security arrangements at Namo Ghat were strict. Indian Air Force officers and jawans were deployed in the helipad area for the morning. Due to security reasons, the movement of the public beyond Phase-2 of Namo Ghat was completely restricted. No person was allowed to go towards the helipad area and security personnel kept sending people back from the designated limit.
