stories.title: Up to ₹5 lakh loan without guarantee at low interest:UP to issue 25 lakh KCCs, disburse ₹2 lakh crore; know how to apply
stories.summary: Monsoon has accelerated farming activity across Uttar Pradesh, prompting the state government to roll out a major initiative to ease farmers' financial burden. The government will issue 2.5 million new Kisan Credit Cards (KCC), enabling eligible farmers to avail crop loans of up to ₹5 lakh at low interest rates without collateral. Similar to how urban consumers use credit cards for daily expenses, the Kisan Credit Card is designed to provide farmers with easy access to credit for farming operations, including the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and other agricultural inputs. KCC will provide protection if crop fails The Kisan Credit Card is not just a loan facility but also serves as a financial safety net during crises. Cardholders are eligible for crop insurance benefits under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). If crops are damaged due to floods, drought, hailstorms or other natural calamities, compensation under the scheme helps farmers repay their bank loans. Loans at 4% interest, no collateral up to ₹2 lakh Launched in August 1998, the Kisan Credit Card scheme earlier offered crop loans of up to ₹3 lakh. The limit has now been increased to ₹5 lakh. For animal husbandry and fisheries, the collateral-free loan limit has also been raised from ₹1.6 lakh to ₹2 lakh. Crop loans under KCC are sanctioned at an interest rate of 7%. However, farmers who repay the loan within one year after harvesting receive a 3% interest subsidy from the government, reducing the effective interest rate to just 4% annually. In cases of natural disasters such as floods or droughts, interest may also be waived or reduced. Banks do not charge any hidden fees on KCC crop loans of up to ₹3 lakh. Processing fees and inspection charges are completely waived. As per NABARD guidelines, a Kisan Credit Card remains valid for five years. Farmers who repay on time become eligible for a 10% annual increase in their credit limit. For example, a ₹1 lakh limit in the first year increases to ₹1.10 lakh in the second year. Special provisions for small farmers Small farmers cultivating limited land can avail loans ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 through the Kisan Credit Card. The amount can be used for cultivation, post-harvest expenses and purchasing small agricultural equipment. Around 76% of all KCC holders currently belong to the small and marginal farmer category. In Uttar Pradesh, the scheme is not limited to crop cultivators. Dairy farmers, goat rearers, poultry farmers and fish farmers are also eligible. Out of 5.59 million applications received from the animal husbandry sector, 5.508 million have been approved so far. Similarly, 677,000 of the 683,000 applications from the fisheries sector have received approval. Apply by filling just one form The government has simplified and digitised the KCC application process. Farmers now need to fill only a single-page application form. For PM-Kisan beneficiaries, several details are already pre-filled. Applications can also be submitted through Common Service Centres (CSCs). The Kisan Rin Portal, launched in September 2023, has significantly accelerated the application and approval process. Scheme available through 457 banks A total of 457 banks across India are part of the Kisan Credit Card scheme, including 37 commercial banks, 46 regional rural banks and 374 cooperative banks. Nearly 200 million applications have been received so far, with cooperative banks accounting for the highest share. Apart from crop loans, KCC holders also receive accident insurance benefits. In case of the cardholder's death or permanent disability, the family is entitled to ₹50,000. Partial disability is covered up to ₹25,000. The premium is nominal and is deducted directly by the bank. Three important questions about Kisan Credit Card Can tenant farmers apply for KCC? Yes. As per NABARD guidelines, sharecroppers, tenant farmers and those cultivating leased land are also eligible. They can apply individually through self-declaration or as part of a group. What happens if the loan is not repaid on time? If the loan is not repaid within one year along with interest, the farmer loses the additional 3% interest subsidy and will have to pay the full applicable interest rate of 7% or 9%. Farmers are therefore advised to settle KCC dues after selling their crops each year. What is e-KCC? Earlier, obtaining a Kisan Credit Card used to take 25–30 days. Uttar Pradesh has now introduced a digital e-KCC system, where land records are verified electronically, allowing banks to approve eligible loans within minutes.

stories.title: 23 Ram Mandir donation-counting staff resign:₹10-20 notes increase, ₹500 notes decline in donation; SC to hear case on July 13
stories.summary: Twenty-three employees responsible for counting donations at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya have resigned simultaneously. They said that after the donation theft came to light, the number of ₹10 and ₹20 notes being offered has increased significantly, making the counting process far more time-consuming. Earlier, they used to prepare 70 to 80 bundles of ₹500 notes, allowing the counting to be completed quickly. Now, they barely manage 15 bundles of ₹500 notes. Previously, the work was carried out in two shifts. The employees said each staff member earlier worked six-hour shifts, but the system has now been changed to a single shift from 9 am to 6 pm. While their salaries have remained unchanged, their working hours have increased, prompting them to resign. Only 13 counting staff now remain with the bank. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the Ram Temple donation theft case on 13 July. A three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant will hear the matter. A total of three petitions have been listed, seeking, among other things, a CBI investigation, the formation of a special SIT, and an expert committee to review various aspects of donation management at the temple. The alleged donation theft has also drawn a reaction from Janaki Temple, regarded as the maternal home of Goddess Sita. Janakpur in neighbouring Nepal is traditionally considered the in-laws' home of Lord Ram. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar on Thursday, Mahant Roshan Das said, "I have never seen or heard of such an incident at any temple dedicated to Lord Ram. Ever since I learnt about the alleged donation theft in Ayodhya, I have been deeply distressed and angered. Those responsible must face strict action."

stories.title: Man beaten to death after visiting lover:Girlfriend critically injured; deceased called his mother saying, 'Save me, they'll kill me'
stories.summary: A case of honor killing has come to light in Kaushambi, UP, where a 19-year-old youth was beaten to death with sticks due to a love affair. The youth had secretly gone to meet his 16-year-old girlfriend at her house at 10 PM on Thursday night. Around 12:00 AM, he called his mother and said “Save me... these people will kill me.” When the family members reached the spot, the youth was found lying bleeding on the roadside outside a relative's house. Nearby, his girlfriend was also lying covered in blood. The family members took both of them to the district hospital, where the youth succumbed to his injuries during treatment at 6:00 AM on Friday morning. The girlfriend's treatment is ongoing. When the police arrived at the scene on the information of the relatives, all the girlfriend's family members were found to be absconding. Investigation revealed that on Thursday evening, the girlfriend's family members had caught both of them in an objectionable situation. After which, both were severely beaten and thrown out of the house. Currently, the police have registered a case on the complaint of the relatives and started investigating the matter. A search in underway for the accused. The young man's body has been sent for post-mortem. The incident took place in Mahua Khara village, Manjhanpur Kotwali area, about three kilometers from the district headquarters. Details of the case Shiv Prasad (19), a resident of Manjhanpur Kotwali area, had been in a love affair with a 16-year-old girl from Mahua Khada village for about a year. On Thursday, he had gone to his aunt's house in Chini village, under Saini police station, from where he was returning with ₹50,000. According to family members, he had called around 7:30 PM to inform that he was returning home. During this time, he secretly reached his girlfriend's house around 10 PM to meet her. Late at night, both were present in the house when the girl's family members came to know about it. After this, a dispute started in the house. The deceased's mother, Puniti Devi, said that her son Shiv Prasad called around 12 AM. He said in a panicked voice, "Mom, save me... these people will kill me." Immediately after this, the call disconnected. The relatives immediately reached Mahua Khada village. Around 12:30 AM, Shiv Prasad was found seriously injured on the roadside outside his house. His girlfriend was also lying injured there. Both were immediately taken to the district hospital. During treatment, doctors declared Shiv Prasad dead around 6 AM on Friday morning, while the teenage girl's treatment is ongoing. The police's initial investigation revealed that the girl's family caught both of them and brutally beat them with sticks. Shiv Prasad sustained serious injuries to his head and body. The girl also got injured in the assault. After the incident, the girl's father Rakesh Rajput, along with other family members, fled their home. Elder brother informed the police in the morning On Friday morning around 6 am, the deceased's elder brother Guru Prasad informed the Manjhanpur Kotwali police about the incident. Kotwali in-charge Sunil Singh, CO Sadar Shivank Singh, and police force reached the spot. The forensic team inspected the crime scene and collected evidence. Police are gathering information about the entire incident by questioning local people and family members. The body has been sent for post-mortem. ‘My brother was murdered, action should be taken’ Guru Prasad, the elder brother of the deceased, said, “My brother Shiv Prasad was returning home with money from his aunt's house. He had called and informed that he had reached Udheen village. After that, there was no contact with him at night. He had called his mother at night, he was scared. We are fully confident that my brother has been murdered. Strict action should be taken against the accused.” The mother alleged that Rakesh Rajput, his sons Sachin and Durgesh, and Rakesh's wife Gediyan together beat her son to death. Shiv Prasad used to farm with his father Shiv Prasad used to farm with his father Rambadan. Shiv's girlfriend has two brothers. She has studied up to eighth grade. CO said, ‘Murder happened due to love affair’ CO Sadar Shivank Singh said, Prima facie, the case is related to a love affair. Investigation revealed that the deceased had a love affair with the girl. After the young man arrived there late at night, a dispute occurred and he was assaulted. The seriously injured young man died during treatment, while the girl is injured. The body has been sent for post-mortem. All aspects of the case are being thoroughly investigated. Strict legal action will be taken against the culprits based on the evidence.

stories.title: UP transfers 20 IAS officers, including 8 women:3 removed from key posts within 6 months, Riya Kejriwal sidelined
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government transferred 20 IAS officers late on Thursday night at around 12 am. Among them, eight are women officers. Three female IAS officers were removed from their posts within just six months of their appointment. These include Revenue Department Secretary Sudha Verma, Medical Education Department Secretary and Director General Sarika Mohan, and Inspector General of Registration Neha Sharma. All three officers had received important postings in the transfers carried out on January 1 this year. However, complaints regarding their functioning had reportedly reached the government after they took charge. This is why they were transferred within six months and nine days. Sudha Verma was reportedly having differences with her department’s Principal Secretary Aparna U. She has now been removed from the post and appointed as Labour Commissioner. There were also complaints regarding the functioning of Medical Education Department Secretary and Director General Sarika Mohan. She has been removed and appointed as Inspector General of Registration. Neha Sharma, who was Inspector General of Registration, has been made Secretary and Director General of the Medical Education Department. Along with this, some officers promoted from PCS to IAS have also been given new postings. See the complete list- Riya Kejriwal removed after power crisis The public protests over a severe power crisis and electricity cuts in the Madhyanchal region have resulted in action against Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Managing Director Riya Kejriwal. She has been removed from the post and appointed as Special Secretary, Child Development and Nutrition. Sandeep Bhagia removed, but got prize posting IAS officer Sandeep Bagiya, Additional Commissioner of State Tax Department, Gautam Buddh Nagar, has also been transferred. The 2018-batch IAS officer has been appointed as the Managing Director of Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, a significant post. Around 60 officers of the State Tax Department had complained against Bagiya to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Chief Secretary SP Goel. He was accused of misbehaving with officers. During a meeting on June 14, one officer, Ved Prakash Singh, reportedly fell unconscious after being reprimanded by Bagiya. Deepa Ranjan has not received a good posting even after 3 years Rajya Gramin Aajeevika Mission Managing Director Deepa Ranjan has been transferred after nearly three years. The 2013-batch IAS officer had been serving on the post since September 2023. She has now been appointed as Special Secretary in the Culture Department. Meanwhile, most officers from her batch are currently serving as district magistrates in various districts. Jag Pravesh removed after traders' displeasure Mathura-Vrindavan Municipal Commissioner Jag Pravesh has been removed following resentment among traders. The 2018-batch IAS officer was appointed as the Municipal Commissioner of Mathura-Vrindavan Municipal Corporation in May last year. Recently, an anti-encroachment drive was carried out on Maholi Road under his leadership. During the action, municipal employees seized goods kept outside shops, leading to a confrontation between traders and the municipal commissioner. Traders later launched a protest against him. Meanwhile, employees of the city’s garbage collection company damaged nine graves and trees during a cemetery cleaning drive. The company paid compensation of only Rs 3,300 at the rate of Rs 100 per grave and tree. The cemetery committee expressed its displeasure over the matter. Ballia Chief Development Officer Ojasvi Raj has been appointed as the new Municipal Commissioner of Mathura-Vrindavan. Culture Department work taken back from Vishal Singh Keeping the 2027 elections in mind, the government has taken away the Culture Department responsibilities from Information and Culture Department Director Vishal Singh. Vishal Singh will now focus completely on the Information Department. Meanwhile, Culture Department Special Secretary Sanjay Singh has been appointed as the department’s director. Rakesh Kumar Patel appointed as CDO in Azamgarh Among the 29 officers promoted from PCS to IAS, Lucknow Additional Divisional Commissioner Rakesh Kumar Patel has been appointed as Chief Development Officer (CDO) of Azamgarh. Muzaffarnagar Additional District Magistrate Sanjay Kumar Singh has been appointed as CDO of Etawah. Gonda Additional District Magistrate Alok Kumar has been appointed as CDO of Ballia. Transfer of Etawah CDO Ajay Kumar Gautam Etawah Chief Development Officer Ajay Kumar Gautam has been transferred and appointed as Additional Commissioner, State Tax, Ghaziabad First. The 2020-batch IAS officer had taken charge as Etawah CDO on December 12, 2023.

stories.title: 2 contractual nurses blamed in newborn's death at Lucknow hospital:Senior gynaecologist served show-cause notice
stories.summary: Two contractual staff nurses have been held responsible in the case of a newborn who died after falling to the floor following birth at Lucknow's Lokbandhu Rajnarayan Hospital. Both are likely to be dismissed from service, while a senior gynaecologist has been served a show-cause notice seeking an explanation. The staff called the on-call gynecologist by phone. The doctor did not come. Nor was any regular staff nurse posted in the ward. The investigation committee has covered up these two crucial points. In this matter, the director says that we can only recommend action; the rest is the work of higher officials. Questions raised on investigation The investigation into the case of an infant's death after delivery at Lokbandhu Hospital is under scrutiny. The hospital has 6 gynecologists, i.e., obstetrics and gynecology specialists. There are seven emergency medical officers. There are approximately 20 nursing and OT staff members. Despite having such a large contingent of doctors and nurses, patients are not receiving adequate treatment. During the incident at the hospital on Sunday, was any regular staff nurse deployed or not? If deployed, why was their responsibility not determined? Also, where was the regular doctor? There are allegations that the staff informed the on-call doctor over the phone. After that, did the on-call doctor come on duty? Who provided treatment in the absence of the doctor? Based on these points, neither was action taken against any regular staff nor against the doctor. An attempt has been made to suppress the matter by merely issuing a notice. Report submitted to DG Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak had ordered the completion of the investigation into the infant's death within 24 hours. The Lokbandhu Hospital administration submitted a two-page report to the Director General of Health Department, Dr. Pawan Kumar Arun. Health Director General Dr. Pawan stated that based on the report, two staff nurses have been removed from their jobs. Meanwhile, Dr. Chandrakanta, who was on on-call duty, has been issued a notice and asked to respond. Dr. Chandrakanta has been asked to respond on three points. This includes seeking information about the doctor's presence as well. Heart-wrenching incident occurred on Monday morning Kirti Pal, a resident of Sita Vihar Colony in Ashiana, was admitted to Lokbandhu on Sunday evening after labor pain. Her husband Shubham said that delivery took place in the labor room on Monday morning, where the infant fell on the floor. The infant's condition became critical due to a deep head injury. The price of the negligence of doctors and staff had to be paid by the infant with its life. A post-mortem of the newborn was conducted at the insistence of family members, which confirmed an injury to the head.

stories.title: Champat Rai remains the most powerful figure at Ram Mandir:Close aides control VIP darshan system, oversee accounts holding ₹1,800 crore
stories.summary: Champat Rai's authority is still intact in the Ram Mandir complex. Dainik Bhaskar's investigation has revealed that even after being out of the trust, Champat Rai's influence still prevails in distributing VIP passes. The temple's ₹1800 crore fund, which is in bank accounts, is also being managed by his close associates. This is despite the fact that Champat Rai resigned from the post of General Secretary on 26 June, following allegations of theft of offerings in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. His resignation was also accepted on 6 July. Questions are also being raised about the role of the SIT investigating the case. It is believed that the SIT has given Champat Rai a 'safe exit' in its report. Why did Champat Rai not leave the Ram Janmabhoomi complex? Champat Rai has been living in Ayodhya since 1991. From the temple movement to advocating for the Ram Lalla Virajman case in the Supreme Court, he was one of the most active faces. After the court's decision, when the construction of the grand temple began, he was made the general secretary of the trust. Champat Rai, who was at the center of Ayodhya's Ram politics for almost 35 years, resigned from his post after allegations of theft. However, a big question now arising among people is why is he still living in the Ram Janmabhoomi complex? 1. Champat's 'two close associates' in the operation of bank accounts In the important meeting of the trust held on 6 July, a committee of three people has been formed for the operation of bank accounts. It includes interim General Secretary Krishna Mohan, Engineer Jagdish Afle, and CA Chandan Rai. Out of these, two names directly operate at the behest of Champat Rai. Because they were appointed to assist the trust at the recommendation of Champat Rai himself. According to the rules, not a single rupee can be withdrawn from the bank without the joint signatures of these three. In such a situation, it is feared that Champat Rai can fully influence the trust's treasury and financial decisions even without being in office. 2. Champat's 18 and Gopal's 14 people are issuing VIP passes Free VIP passes are issued for Mangal Aarti, Shringar Aarti, and Shayan Aarti at the Ram Temple. For this, special digital IDs are given to the officials responsible for the trust. The ID of Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra, who resigned on June 26, was deactivated on the same day. The ID of Gopal Nagarkote, who was removed as a special invitee member, was also deactivated on the morning of July 7. However, Champat Rai's ID was active until July 9, which has now been deactivated. Claim: ‘Money is being taken for VIP passes’ Whoever issues VIP passes, what's the problem? We asked this question to journalist Indubhushan Pandey, who has been covering the Ram temple in Ayodhya for a long time. He says there is a racket of VIP pass issuers and hotel owners at the temple, who are earning money even from darshan (worship). VIP passes are free. This is a facility provided for the elderly, women, and children. These passes are issued in six to seven slots a day. One slot, meaning one time period, can issue 300 passes. However, with these IDs, 2,500-3,000 passes can be issued offline every day. Santosh Dubey, founder of Dharmasena, claims devotees are charged between ₹1,000 and ₹3,000. This includes a share for both the hotel and the pass issuer. 3. Who gave Tinnu Yadav authority? In the meeting on 6 July, SIT's nine-page preliminary investigation report was presented. Looking at this report, questions are arising that the entire blame has been placed on Dr. Anil Mishra. The report states that Dr. Anil Mishra did not properly implement the SOP to prevent the theft of offerings. The SOP, which was formulated between the bank and the trust on September 20, 2024, and February 6, 2025, and bore the signatures of the then SBI Manager Govind Mishra and Dr. Anil Mishra, was never implemented on the ground. Pages 6 and 7 of the report mention the suspicious role of Ramshankar alias Tinnu Yadav. Without any written order, the keys to the donation boxes remained with Tinnu. He used to move in and out of the counting room without any hindrance. He had a police-style 'walkie-talkie'. He also had his own VIP pass ID. He used his influence to get his nephew, Manish Yadav, appointed in the counting room, who was caught red-handed stealing on CCTV. The SIT did write in the report that Tinnu Yadav had all these powers. However, it was nowhere written who gave these powers to Tinnu? Everyone in Ayodhya knows that Tinnu Yadav is none other than Champat Rai's driver. Champat Rai himself had made him the all-in-all of the temple's arrangements. Mahipal Singh, who was an accountant in the trust, had claimed that he had already informed Dr. Anil Mishra, Champat Rai, and Gopal Nagarkote about the theft of offerings. However, upon telling the truth, he was fired from his job. The SIT did not even take his statement. Engineer Dinanath Verma had accused Dr. Anil Mishra of commission-taking in temple construction materials and 40% of the works. He had complained about this to Champat Rai. After the complaint, he was first assigned to count the offering money. Then, he was threatened and driven out of Ayodhya. The SIT did not deem it necessary to interrogate him either.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes 30 UP cities, canal breaches:Graveyard soil washes away in Saharanpur, water enters Banda homes
stories.summary: The monsoon has gathered pace across Uttar Pradesh. Since 5 am on Friday, intermittent rain has been reported in 30 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur and Prayagraj. The remaining districts are under cloudy skies, with cool winds prevailing. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain and thunderstorm alert for 49 districts today. In the state capital, Lucknow, heavy rain that began on Thursday afternoon continued until Friday morning. Light showers persisted throughout the night. The rain stopped at around 6:15 am, but dark clouds continued to hover over the city. Around 45 minutes later, the sky darkened again and drizzle resumed. People were seen on the roads carrying umbrellas and wearing raincoats. In Bijnor, heavy rainfall caused the wall of a government school to collapse. Varanasi and Pratapgarh witnessed waterlogging in streets and lanes, while several parts of Hapur were inundated with up to two feet of water. In view of the adverse weather, schools up to Class 12 have been closed in 13 districts, including Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Ghaziabad. Over the past 48 hours, 12 people have lost their lives in weather-related incidents. In Sambhal, a woman was killed in a road accident. In Hardoi, two sisters who had gone to bathe in a river were swept away by the strong current. A farmer managed to rescue one of them, while the other remains missing. In Saharanpur, three people, including a woman, were swept away along with their motorcycle in the swollen Sahenshra River, but were rescued by local villagers. CM directs officials to be on the ground Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken cognisance of the deaths caused by heavy rainfall and lightning strikes. He has instructed officials to assess the damage and provide compensation within 24 hours. The Chief Minister directed officials to visit the affected areas, reach out to families impacted by the incidents, and provide all possible assistance. Yogi also wished a speedy recovery for those injured. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: “The rain-bearing system that developed over the Bay of Bengal has now reached the vicinity of Madhya Pradesh. Its impact is also being felt in Uttar Pradesh, due to which the monsoon has intensified across the state. The rainfall spell is expected to continue for the next five days.”

stories.title: Retired ARTO concealed valuables in secret vaults:₹20 crore in gold bars, biscuits and diamond-studded jewellery found
stories.summary: Retired Assistant Regional Transport Officer (ARTO) Lalit Kumar has been found to possess assets worth ₹35 crore so far. The Vigilance team found gold, silver, and diamonds kept in safes in his house. This action is not the result of a single day's investigation. It began six years ago with a complaint made during Lalit's posting in Kanpur. Despite the completion of the investigation, approval for action was not received from the government during the Lok Sabha elections 2024. Approval was granted after the elections. Subsequently, an FIR was filed. Then, with a search warrant from the court, the Vigilance team raided Lalit's residence in Aliganj, Lucknow, on July 7 and 8. Notes and jewellery were also found from small safes built into the walls According to sources from the Vigilance team, in addition to the main safes, small inbuilt safes were also built into the walls of the house. During the search, the team meticulously inspected every room and wall, uncovering these hidden safes. They contained cash, gold jewellery, and important documents. Investigation officers opened each safe, matched its contents, and prepared a list of recovered items. Only Lalit had knowledge of these secret safes. The safe had an automatic lock, could not be opened for two hours When the Vigilance team reached Lalit Kumar's house, the biggest challenge was opening the automatic lock safe kept in the house. Officials repeatedly asked for the password to open the safe, but Lalit Kumar kept saying that he didn't remember it. Due to this, the search operation was stuck for about two hours. Later, with technical assistance and by following the necessary procedure, the safe was opened. Gold and Silver Biscuits Found in Safe As soon as the safe was opened, gold and silver biscuits, bricks, and a large quantity of diamond-studded jewelry were found inside. The team prepared a list of all the items. A government-recognised valuer was called to assess the items. The value of the recovered gold, silver, and jewellery was estimated to be around ₹20 crore. According to officials, the team was also surprised to find such a large quantity of precious metals and jewellery at once. 'Secret Spots' were made in beds, walls, false panels, and furniture During the search, the Vigilance team did not limit itself to only cupboards and lockers. Beds, walls, false panels, furniture, and even the storeroom were thoroughly inspected. During this, several hidden places were found where cash and valuables were kept. Officials say that during the search, with every new recovery, the team kept finding new 'secret spots'. Due to this, the search operation lasted for several hours. All the recovered items were listed and seized for further investigation. Notes and jewellery hidden in packets After the safe was opened, Vigilance meticulously searched the entire house again. From different rooms, cupboards, and other places in the house, ₹1.62 crore in cash, property deeds, bank investments, mutual funds, fixed deposits, and other financial documents, hidden in packets, were recovered. In this operation, which lasted for about nine hours, the scope of assets expanded with every new recovery. Now, investigation agencies are trying to find out from what sources these assets were acquired and whether any organised network was active behind this. Investigation was approved in 2020 Lalit Kumar was posted as Divisional Inspector (Technical) in the Kanpur RTO office when a complaint of disproportionate assets against him reached the government. After a preliminary inquiry, the Transport Commissioner, Uttar Pradesh, granted permission for a detailed investigation to the Anti-Corruption Bureau on September 11, 2020. Subsequently, records of his income, expenses, bank accounts, properties, and investments were scrutinised. Investigation reveals 73.6 per cent more expenditure than income During the investigation, the agency found that Lalit Kumar's legitimate income was ₹93.26 lakh, while his expenditure on the purchase, maintenance of movable and immovable properties, and other items reached ₹1.61 crore. This means he spent ₹68.66 lakh more than his declared income, which was approximately 73.6 per cent of his legitimate income. According to investigation officials, he could not provide a satisfactory explanation for this additional expenditure. Action stalled during Lok Sabha elections According to sources, after the investigation was completed, the process of approval at the government level for action against him was underway in 2024. During this period, the Model Code of Conduct for the Lok Sabha elections came into effect, which affected the administrative process and the prosecution's permission could not be issued on time. After the elections were completed and necessary approvals were received, an FIR was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the investigation was handed over to Vigilance, Lucknow Sector. Search operation conducted for 2 days with court warrant During the investigation, Vigilance obtained a search warrant from the court. Subsequently, a search operation was conducted on July 7 and 8, 2026, at the residence located in Aliganj, Lucknow. During the search, approximately 1.62 crore rupees in cash, hidden in packets in different parts of the house, were recovered. The search yielded approximately 13 kg of gold biscuits and jewellery, and about 9 kg of silver biscuits and jewelry. A government valuer has estimated their value at approximately 20 crore rupees. Documents related to bank accounts, post office, mutual funds, fixed deposits, and other investments worth more than one crore rupees were also found. Now the agency is also investigating whether any other person or network was involved in acquiring such a large number of asset. Properties found in Lucknow, Noida, Barabanki and Raebareli During the investigation, the vigilance team found documents for 15 immovable properties, including residential buildings, plots, agricultural land, and flat bookings, in Lucknow, Barabanki, Raebareli, and Noida. The estimated value of these properties is said to be around 13 crore rupees. Records of two cars, a revolver, and heavy expenses incurred on home furnishings have also been included in the investigation.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft sparks concern in Nepal:Janakpur Mandir to send 7-member team to Ayodhya, demands strict action
stories.summary: The alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has upset devotees in Janakpur, Nepal, believed to be the birthplace of Goddess Sita and Lord Ram's in-laws' home. Mahant Roshan Das of the Janaki Temple said he had never heard of such an incident at any Ram temple and called for strict action against those responsible. He said the temple had contacted Ayodhya to check on the situation. A team of five to seven people from Janakpur is now likely to visit Ayodhya during the holy month of Sawan to express support, offer prayers and return. VHP Dhanusha district president Santosh Shah said people in Janakpur were deeply hurt by the news. Janakpur Mayor Manoj Shah said Ayodhya authorities had assured them that all the gifts sent during the Ram Mandir consecration are safe in the temple museum. Gifts sent from Janakpur during the Ram Mandir consecration During the Ram Mandir consecration in January 2024, Janakpur sent gifts symbolising Sita's griha pravesh (homecoming). Mahant Roshan Das had travelled to Ayodhya with around 500 devotees in three trucks, seven buses and 40 SUVs. The offerings included: Ayodhya: Smaller notes increase after donation theft, making counting harder Abhinav Anand Singh There has been a big difference in the amount of donations received at the Shri Ram temple. Officials involved in counting temple donations said the mix of cash offerings has changed significantly after the alleged theft. Earlier, donations often included 70-80 bundles of ₹500 notes, making counting faster. Now, ₹10 and ₹20 notes have increased sharply, while only about 15 bundles of ₹500 notes are being received. The cash collected from 54 donation boxes is sent in six large containers to the counting centre. Staff said the higher number of small notes has made the counting process much slower. Resignations leave donation counting staff short The donation counting system is also facing a staff shortage after 23 counting personnel resigned over salary issues and longer working hours. Only 13 counting staff remain, raising concerns over delays in counting donations. Earlier, the work was done in two six-hour shifts. Now, employees work a single shift from 9 am to 6 pm. The counting work is being carried out through SBI. Akhilesh Yadav seeks probe into temple workers' call records Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has demanded an investigation into the call detail records of everyone working at the Ram Mandir. He claimed that "99.9%" of the people working there would have links with the BJP and said the records should be examined as part of the investigation.

Brown claimed he lost his passport in Thailand and traveled to India by sea. He had been residing in Goa and Bengaluru before his apprehension. Officials are investigating his claims and lack of documentation.

stories.summary: Hilaria Baldwin suggests using breath for greater awareness and clarity. Conscious breathing creates a pause, allowing for observation instead of instinct. This pause helps overcome ego and old destructive patterns effectively. Modern research supports slower breathing for stress reduction and relaxation. This simple technique aids in making better decisions in daily life.

stories.title: 'Your life matters to us': Mahua Moitra urges Sonam Wangchuk to end fast as hunger strike enters Day 17
stories.summary: Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra urged Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike. Wangchuk's fast against examination irregularities reached sixteen days. stories.summary: Nine European countries and Ukraine established a coalition for defensive anti-ballistic capabilities. This alliance aims to deter and defeat future missile threats effectively. The group will integrate defense industries, research, and operational experiences. Ukrainian President Zelensky attended a Paris meeting to reaffirm support for his nation. This initiative responds to growing ballistic missile threats and Ukraine's unique experiences.

stories.title: LeT, IS operatives among 34 killed in Khuzdar attack: BLA
stories.summary: The Baloch Liberation Army claimed a major suicide attack on an ISIS-K commander's compound. This operation targeted a meeting coordinating efforts against the Baloch political movement. The BLA stated that 34 operatives, including ISIS and LeT members, were killed. The attack, executed by the Majeed Brigade, followed weeks of intelligence surveillance. This incident highlights alleged links between Pakistan's ISI and militant groups.

stories.title: Why did Tom Segura and Christina P separate after their 18-year marriage? Podcasters’ split details emerge
stories.summary: Tom Segura and Christina P have reportedly separated after 18 years of marriage, according to TMZ. The news has surprised many fans who have followed the couple’s journey through comedy, podcasts and television projects. While the pair have remained largely private about the situation, reports suggest they will continue working together, leaving plenty of questions still unanswered.

stories.title: “He was punching me”: Ria Jalesa accuses Beyoncé’s nephew Julez Smith of hotel assault, says she was left with bruises
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Ria Jalesa has accused Julez Smith, Beyoncé’s nephew and Solange Knowles’ son, of physically assaulting her during a hotel encounter. She claims he left her with bruises, damaged her phone, pointed a firearm at her, and threatened her life. Ria shared her allegations in livestreams, while Smith has not publicly responded so far.

stories.title: Social media platforms must follow SOPs on child abuse content: Government
stories.summary: Social media platforms must follow child abuse material reporting rules. Timely reporting and coordination with law enforcement are key duties. The government is examining Meta's response to Instagram ad concerns. Officials focus on platform compliance with material detection obligations. Lapses in procedures will invite action under applicable legal frameworks.

stories.title: NMC plans ban on medical seat hike if buildings not yet complete
stories.summary: Medical colleges must have full infrastructure before seeking seat increases. Incomplete applications will be rejected without any chance for correction. A mandatory corpus fund will be fixed by the Medical Assessment and Rating Board. Institutions influencing the NMC face application rejection or suspension. These draft amendments are now open for public consultation.

stories.title: ED: IBC norms misused for laundering in RCFL cases
stories.summary: The IBBI cancelled Chandra Prakash Jain's registration as a resolution professional. This action followed an ED probe into ten insolvency cases linked to Reliance Commercial Finance. The investigation revealed Jain allegedly ignored significant financial red flags and due diligence requirements. The IBBI stated the IBC framework was misused for tax avoidance and money laundering. Creditors received only Rs 30 lakh against admitted claims totaling Rs 1,433 crore.

stories.title: Kharif acreage falls 16%, but ethanol effect boosts sugarcane
stories.summary: Overall kharif crop acreage has fallen sixteen percent as of last Friday. Sugarcane acreage, however, has increased despite water resource pressures. Pulses and cereals show the highest decline in sown area this season. Farmers continue to favor cash crops for better market prices. This trend supports government ethanol initiatives and reduces import bills.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust invites CEO applications: Must be a 'practising Hindu, Ram bhakt'
stories.summary: The Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra trust is seeking applications for its first chief executive officer. This professional role aims to enhance the management of the Ayodhya Ram temple operations. The trust decided to appoint a CEO after recent allegations of donation theft by cash-counting agents. Applications are open for eligible Hindu candidates with extensive managerial experience. The new CEO will report to the trust's general secretary and oversee daily functions.

stories.title: AAP launches signature drive to seek death for Ayodhya donation thieves
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal has initiated a nationwide signature campaign demanding capital punishment for those accused of theft. He launched the drive in Delhi, signing an open letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Kejriwal urged citizens to organize Hanuman Chalisa recitations and gather signatures for the letter. Delhi BJP functionary Praveen Kapoor stated the campaign aims to defame the Ram Mandir.

stories.title: UK: Peterborough council denies sale of Hindu temple to mosque is ‘unlawful’
stories.summary: Peterborough city council argued its decision to sell a complex housing a Hindu temple was not unlawful. The council stated that while Hindu faith is protected, it does not dictate decisions. The Hindu community expressed disbelief at the council's valuation of alternative premises. The council needs the money from the sale to the UK Islamic Mission. Bharat Hindu Samaj is seeking a judicial review to quash the council's decision.

stories.title: Meet the magnetic liquid metal robot: It merges and squeezes through tiny gaps like a living cell
One Indian crew member killed, 6 injured after Iran strikes UAE tankers in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Two UAE-flagged tankers were struck by Iranian cruise missiles in Omani waters. One Indian crew member died and eight others sustained injuries in the attack. The UAE condemned the incident as a serious violation of international law. This escalation occurs amid rising military tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The US Central Command also launched new strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Citing former PM Manmohan Singh, BJP says Congress has habit of discrediting Election Commission
stories.summary: The BJP cited Manmohan Singh's remarks to accuse Congress of attacking institutions. Congress countered by referencing Quraishi's book to criticize Prime Minister Modi. The BJP alleged ministers targeted the poll body when the UPA was in power. Salman Khurshid was censured for promising an enhanced Muslim quota during a campaign. Singh viewed the EC as democracy's soul, while Modi sees it as a political tool.

stories.title: Anti-graft bills not aimed at undercutting non-BJP governments, says ministry of home affairs
stories.summary: The home ministry has rejected opposition claims regarding anti-corruption bills. These proposed laws aim to remove arrested officials after thirty days in custody. Legislative membership remains intact, ensuring government stability is unaffected. The ministry asserts the mandate is protected by ensuring effective and trustworthy governance. Parliamentary committees are scrutinizing these proposed anti-corruption measures.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Ram mandir fund probe status report in a week
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is now overseeing the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation embezzlement probe. It has directed the UP government's Special Investigation Team to submit a status report. The court is considering multiple public interest litigations seeking independent investigations. The probe has already led to the arrest of eight individuals involved in suspicious activities. Further hearings on this matter are scheduled for July 20.

stories.title: 'Comprehensive sex education' coming soon to schools, government tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: India will formally introduce comprehensive sex education in schools and colleges nationwide. The government has accepted a committee's report recommending this significant curriculum change. This move aims to address concerns regarding adolescent pregnancies and criminalization under the Pocso Act. Subjects like child sexual abuse and safety will be integrated from foundational stages. The National Council of Educational Research and Training will develop the new curriculum.

stories.title: India launches UNSC campaign for 2028-29 term, Jaishankar unveils ‘SHANTI’ vision
stories.summary: India officially launched its campaign for a United Nations Security Council seat. External affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted the country's peacekeeping and development partnerships. India presented its SHANTI vision for global governance and cooperation among nations. The nation seeks support for its candidature amid a changing global landscape. India previously served eight terms as a non-permanent Security Council member.

Supreme Court quashes Guwahati high court order on 27 'foreigners'
stories.summary: The Supreme Court stressed fair procedures for declaring individuals foreign nationals. It found fault with tribunals and the Guwahati High Court's actions. Many orders were quashed as they lacked hearings for affected people. The court directed tribunals to provide fresh hearings and reconsider cases. This ensures lawful adjudication and protects constitutional rights for all.

stories.title: Clavicular claims Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's advisers suggested a gym livestream to reach younger voters
stories.summary: A streamer named Clavicular claims Netanyahu's advisers sought his help. They reportedly wanted a gym livestream to improve the leader's image. Clavicular stated advisers believed Netanyahu appeared old and out of shape. This claim remains unverified by any official confirmation. A meeting with an adviser was confirmed at a nightclub.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Dale Carnegie: "Don't be afraid of enemies who attack you. Be afraid of…" - why honest criticism is more valuable than praise
stories.summary: Dale Carnegie cautioned against trusting flattering friends more than open enemies. He argued that sincere criticism offers valuable lessons for personal growth. Flattery creates a false sense of security, hindering honest self-reflection. As influence grows, people often avoid challenging powerful individuals. Seeking truthful feedback remains crucial for lasting judgment and improvement.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: 18 Amarnath yatris injured in Ramban multi-vehicle collision
stories.summary: Eighteen pilgrims sustained injuries in a multi-vehicle collision involving several buses and a car. The accident occurred on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in Ramban district early Monday. All injured pilgrims were promptly taken to the Ramban district hospital for treatment. They had sustained only minor injuries and were reported to be in stable condition. Police have initiated an investigation into the cause of the unfortunate pile-up.

stories.summary: The BJP has issued a Rs 100-crore defamation notice to Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. This action follows Abdullah's allegations that a BJP functionary attempted to poach his party MLA. The notice demands an unconditional public apology from Abdullah within seven days. Abdullah dismissed the notice, viewing it as a sign of his political significance. He also warned of legal counter-notices against BJP functionaries for their past statements.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marcus Aurelius: 'The only wealth which you will keep forever is the wealth...'
stories.summary: The philosophical musings of ancient Roman thinkers reveal that genuine wealth stems from the act of giving. Unlike material possessions, which fade over time, generosity fosters enduring character and deep social connections. This age-old wisdom stands in stark contrast to the practice of hoarding, which provides merely an illusion of security. Today, embracing generosity mirrors contemporary charitable endeavors and strategic investments, ultimately converting fleeting assets into lasting positive impact.

stories.title: ‘Democratic decentralisation’: Government announces hill councils for all 7 Ladakh districts
stories.summary: Ladakh will establish hill development councils in all seven districts to strengthen grassroots governance. This move aims to decentralize power and improve administrative reach across the vast territory. Currently, only Leh and Kargil districts have these autonomous district councils. Discussions are ongoing for a unique UT-level legislative body with broad powers. A draft framework for this new arrangement will be prepared soon.

stories.title: Quote of the Day by Napoleon Bonaparte: 'Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake'
stories.summary: The concept of strategic patience can provide a significant edge in competitive environments. By letting rivals make their own missteps, one can capitalize on the ensuing turmoil. Historical figures like Napoleon Bonaparte utilized this method effectively at the Battle of Austerlitz. In contemporary business and political arenas, this approach highlights the importance of timing and self-restraint rather than hasty actions.

stories.title: Kai Cenat drops ‘EBK’ diss track targeting FunnyMike, DDG, Rakai and other Streamer University critics
stories.summary: Kai Cenat has released a diss track titled EBK, targeting creators who criticized his event. The song addresses complaints about the Streamer University 2026 selection process. FunnyMike and DDG were specifically called out in the new track. This online feud continues as the event approaches its scheduled start. Fans anticipate further responses from involved creators and critics.

The analysis of fossilized bones uncovered a diet rich in fish, prompting a reevaluation of wolf domestication theories and illustrating a nuanced history of human-canine interactions.

stories.title: Quote of the day by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe: "My opinion is that politicians should be humble in the face of history. stories.summary: Authorities restricted access to Srinagar's Martyrs' Graveyard on Monday. Political leaders paid homage at their respective party offices instead. stories.title: Steve Jobs' widow Laurene grew up lower middle class, but now spends summers aboard superyacht
stories.summary: Laurene Powell Jobs navigated financial hardships during her childhood in rural New Jersey. While Apple faced initial economic challenges, it eventually soared in profitability. Today, the luxurious superyacht Venus stands as a testament to her extraordinary success.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Roger Federer: "I'm as patient a father as I am on the tennis court. It takes a lot for me to get really upset, but…"
stories.summary: Roger Federer admits parenting tests his renowned patience, which is usually seen on court. He acknowledges that children can indeed provoke frustration, even in calm individuals. This honest confession removes unrealistic expectations many parents place upon themselves. Patience involves responding with care even after frustration arises, not pretending it never happens. Federer's experience shows that professional success does not exempt anyone from ordinary family life.

Efforts are underway to identify and apprehend the motorcycle-borne attacker.

This move aims to protect American citizens from international prosecution.

The court has sought a response from Tihar Jail authorities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Muhammad Ali, "The Greatest": "I try not to speak about all the charities and people I help, because…" - a timeless lesson reveals that the purest acts of kindness are often the ones no one ever sees
stories.summary: Muhammad Ali believed true generosity requires no expectation of return. He deliberately avoided publicizing his extensive charitable work and humanitarian efforts. This approach highlighted his commitment to helping others without seeking personal recognition. The article emphasizes that quiet acts of kindness often carry the most significant impact. Ali's perspective remains relevant in today's highly visible world.

stories.summary: The mortal remains of fifteen Indian tourists who died in Vietnam have arrived in Mumbai. State governments will coordinate the transportation of bodies to their final destinations. Vietnamese authorities and citizens provided significant support following the tragic boat accident. Sixteen rescued Indian tourists have already returned to India safely. One injured Indian national remains hospitalized in Ho Chi Minh City.

stories.title: This supersonic jet needed a radiation meter because it flew twice as high as commercial aircraft
stories.summary: The Concorde jet soared near the edge of space, requiring careful monitoring of radiation levels to ensure passenger safety. In the face of hazardous cosmic storms, pilots were mandated to descend to safer altitudes. While this supersonic aircraft typically flew above the majority of Earth's atmospheric shield, fluctuations in radiation exposure depended on several factors including altitude, geography, and solar activity. During such storms, safety took precedence over speed.

stories.title: Scientists say crushing deep-ocean pressure squeezes hidden nutrients out of sinking marine snow, feeding microbes and changing what we know about Earth’s carbon cycle
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the immense pressure in the deep ocean squeezes nutrients out of sinking marine snow—tiny particles of dead algae and organic matter—providing an unexpected food source for deep-sea microbes. The findings suggest more carbon escapes into deep ocean water than previously believed, which could reshape scientists' understanding of Earth's carbon cycle and improve future climate models.

Current revenue streams are generated through carbon removal and biodiversity credits, with aspirations to draw significant investments for sustainable environmental solutions.

stories.summary: Earth's plant life may persist for approximately 1.8 billion more years. The Sun's increasing brightness will gradually make conditions too harsh for vegetation. Hardy plant species adapted to extreme conditions will likely be the last survivors. This slow fading of life contrasts with dramatic disaster movie endings. The planet's eventual uninhabitability will unfold over an immense stretch of time.

stories.summary: The Indian Army has requested organic pulses for its personnel, initiating a pilot program. Government cooperatives Nafed and NCCF will identify sources and manage the supply chain. This move aims to encourage farmers to produce organic pulses with assured demand. Organic pulses offer health benefits and require careful handling and certification. The pilot program will establish an institutional requirement for sustainable nutrition within the force.

stories.title: A supernova lit up Earth’s sky in 1054 and was visible in daylight. Hubble now shows its glowing remains are still expanding nearly 1,000 years later
stories.summary: Astronomers used the Hubble Space Telescope to measure the expanding Crab Nebula. New images compared with older ones show gas filaments moving outwards. This ancient stellar explosion's remnant is still actively changing today. The Crab Pulsar at the center continues to power the nebula's glow. Scientists also identified previously unrecognised filament structures within the nebula.

stories.summary: A Delhi court convicted former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and others for murder. The court found Hussain guilty of murder and rioting charges related to the 2020 riots. Arguments on the quantum of sentence will be heard later.

stories.summary: A journalist moved from Los Angeles to San Francisco for an AI startup role. She found a work culture focused on building products and new technology. Her journalism skills proved valuable in explaining complex AI concepts to a wider audience. While missing her home, she embraced this significant technological shift. She is grateful for the unexpected opportunity which changed her career path.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott is still worth $33 billion after giving away $10 million a day for seven years
stories.summary: MacKenzie Scott, a prominent philanthropist, skillfully balances her substantial wealth with a commitment to giving away billions each year. Scott's unique approach involves providing unrestricted grants to organizations, a strategy that, while criticized by some tech moguls, far surpasses their charitable efforts.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Snoop Dogg: ‘You can take your boy out the hood but you can't take the hood out the homie’
stories.summary: The influence of our surroundings extends far beyond mere memories, deeply embedding in our character and daily behaviors. Our formative settings mold not only our speech and desires but also our fundamental instincts. Even as we advance in life, these early lessons remain pivotal, guiding our perceptions and interactions. This ongoing relationship underscores the importance of integrating past experiences as we navigate new paths in life.
